課程簡介:
全球政治思想史（Global Political Thought）：
洛克與現代世界的形成
建議先修過西洋政治思想史或類似課程。
本課程以十七世紀英國思想家約翰．洛克（
John Locke
）為核心，探討近代政治與宗教思想如何在科學革命、宗教衝突、大西洋殖民擴張與近代革命的歷史脈絡中形成與發展。課程將首先從法蘭西斯培根（
Francis Bacon
）的《新大西島》（
New Atlantis
）出發，考察近代知識觀與政治秩序的關係，進而閱讀洛克《政府論次講》、《論宗教寬容》，以及與殖民治理相關文本，分析自由、財產、宗教寬容、殖民與政治權威等核心議題。課程後半將進一步討論當代洛克研究的重要論爭，包括殖民主義命題（
the colonial thesis
）、洛克思想在大西洋世界的傳播，以及其對美國革命與近代自由主義的影響。透過經典文本與當代研究成果的對話，本課程將引導學生理解洛克政治思想與當代不同詮釋與批判之意義，以及政治思想如何展現近代政治世界的形成。
課程目標與學習成效:
課程目標與學習成效
本課程旨在培養學生閱讀近代政治思想經典文本的能力，並理解政治思想如何回應其所處的歷史與宗教脈絡。完成本課程後學生應能：
理解十七世紀科學革命、殖民擴張等脈絡，以及其對近代政治思想形成的影響。
掌握近代重要政治思想家與政治家洛克的整體政治思想，並有能力分析自由、財產權、宗教寬容、政治權威與殖民主義等核心政治概念。
認識近年洛克研究的重要學術論爭，包括殖民主義命題、共和主義與自由主義之爭，以及洛克思想在大西洋世界與美國革命中的傳播與接受。

課程簡介:
這門課程從國際政治思想的視角，考察十八世紀中葉至二十世紀初「帝國」、「文明」與「演化」如何成為理解世界政治秩序的重要概念。近代世界並非僅由形式上並列的國家所構成；帝國、殖民地與不同形式的政治依附長期存在，而「文明程度」、「政治能力」與「社會發展」亦經常被用來解釋乃至規範不同政治共同體在世界秩序中的位置。
我們從休謨對商業、文明與政治社會發展的論述出發，分析十八世紀政治思想如何逐漸形成一套比較不同社會與政治制度的歷史語言。邊沁有關殖民地、立法與法典化的著作，則使我們得以考察效益主義的普遍主義理想如何進入帝國與跨地域治理的問題。詹姆斯・穆勒與約翰・穆勒的文本進一步呈現政府形式、代議政治與殖民統治之間的緊張關係：政治自由是否具有普遍適用性，往往取決於思想家如何判斷一個社會的文明狀態與政治能力。
十九世紀中葉的演化思想進一步改變了理解國際政治差異的方式。透過史賓塞，本課程討論社會演化如何提供一套跨越國界的比較架構，卻也推導出反帝國擴張的激進立場。課程最後閱讀梁啟超的《新民說》，考察文明與演化的政治語言進入東亞之後，如何在帝國競爭與民族國家形成的脈絡中被重新詮釋和轉譯。梁啟超所面對的並非抽象的現代化問題，而是如何使一個政治共同體取得在國際秩序中生存與自主的資格。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程旨在培養學生從國際政治思想的角度閱讀現代政治思想經典，理解政治思想不僅處理一國之內的政府、自由與制度問題，也持續回應不同政治共同體如何共存、支配與被分類的世界政治問題。學生將掌握帝國、文明與演化等概念如何介入對國際秩序的理解，並分析政治思想家如何論證和解釋不同社會之間的不平等政治關係。
本課程著重政治普遍主義與國際政治差序之間的張力。透過休謨、邊沁、詹姆斯・穆勒與約翰・穆勒的文本，學生將分析自由、良善政府、文明、自治與法律改革等政治原則，在面對殖民地與非歐洲社會時如何被調整、限制或重新論證。課程並不預設自由主義與帝國主義之間存在單一、固定的關係，而是要求學生從具體文本辨識不同的帝國論證及其內部矛盾。本課程亦將演化思想視為現代國際政治思想的重要組成部分。學生將理解社會演化論如何建立一種特殊的動態歷史觀，而此種歷史觀又與帝國擴張存在何種關係。此外，本課程將十九世紀英國政治思想與晚清中國思想置於同一問題史脈絡中。透過梁啟超對國民、進化與文明競爭的思考，學生將分析政治概念跨越語言與政治空間時所發生的轉譯與重構。
課程最終希望學生能超越以「西方思想影響中國」為中心的單向敘事，從全球思想史與國際政治思想的角度，理解不同政治社會如何在不對稱的世界秩序中重新界定自身。例如，十九世紀歐洲的進步與演化論述如何進入晚清中國，又如何在帝國競爭、民族危機及國家建構的迫切條件下，轉化為梁啟超所提出的「新民」問題。透過此種跨脈絡比較，學生將具備初步的概念史、全球思想史及國際政治思想研究能力。

課程目標與學習成效: 課程目標在於培養學生對民主理論與實踐的系統性理解，並透過跨國比較視角，掌握影響民主發展與穩定的關鍵因素。完成本課程後，學生將能夠 1) 解釋民主化與民主鞏固的主要理論與爭議；2) 分析不同國家的民主經驗與制度差異；3) 理解當代民主倒退的核心特徵及背後原因；4) 閱讀並批判性思考具實證基礎的比較政治學研究。

Students will explore multidisciplinary perspectives on human rights institutions and jurisprudence. Method, Requirements, & Assignments
The seminar comprises a combination of lectures, guided readings, and discussions.
Google Classroom Participation #so4fv67w
All students must join the course communication platform and enable notifications. To join it, please first set up your NCCU Google Workspace account via personal settings in iNCCU https://i.nccu.edu.tw.
Designated Readings and Rapporteur Podcast
-
Structure & Format
: Each rapporteur team—consisting of 3 members from diverse cultural and disciplinary backgrounds—will produce a 20-minute AUDIO PODCAST summarising the week's designated readings. Podcasts must be uploaded to Google Classroom at least 24 hours before class.
-
Objective
: This assignment is an exercise in audio-only storytelling. The goal is to translate dense academic literature or case law into an accessible, engaging narrative without relying on slides or visual aids.
Mid-term Oral Examination (Individual Session)
-
Scheduling
: The presentation order will be randomly generated and published one week prior to the examination.
-
Format
: On the day of the exam, each student will draw a random question and will have 20 minutes to prepare the response, during which open-resource research, references, and peer consultations are fully permitted.
-
Presentation
: Each student will deliver a 3-minute oral response to the instructor. Please note that this is a Socratic-style examination; the instructor may interrupt students’ presentations at any point with follow-up questions.
Term Oral Examination (Moot Court Session)
-
Structure
: Rapporteur teams will be organised into different rounds of moot court simulation, playing either the applicant council or the respondent State (assignment to be determined randomly).
-
Materials & Rules
: Case facts and simplified oral arguments rules will be published on Google Classroom by late November.
-
Requirements
: Robust invocation and citation of the course jurisprudence are essential. Written memorials are only required to be communicated to the opposing party team.

課程簡介: 本課程冀為大專同學提供認識台灣環境治理與永續發展的知識，從政治面、經濟面以及都市規劃面，來檢視達成永續發展政策目標的挑戰，以培養同學成為具環保意識與智能的中堅，共同為台灣與世界的環境保護。環保除了是技術問題，亦為政策與行政的問題，更是生活切身的問題：從自身健康的維護，到對於一支草一點露的珍惜，再到對於瀕危物種的關心，最後到付諸行動，參與政府政策過程以追求經濟發展與環境保護的均衡，並將資源作合理、恰當的分配，讓環境弱勢團體獲得公平的對待，最後發展相關制度與行政措施，以有效利用有限資源，鼓勵全民參與志願性的環境保護工作等，都是值得我們瞭解的議題。

課程簡介: 本課程提供對美國政治研究的廣泛導論，重點聚焦於聯邦政府的核心政治機構與公民的政治行為。我們將從詹姆斯‧麥迪遜（James Madison）在《聯邦黨人文集》（Federalist）第10與第51號文件中所描述的憲法邏輯作為課程起點。這套「麥迪遜式」（Madisonian）政府模型將作為我們研究的參照標準，協助我們評估美國憲政體制是否依此運作，若否，問題又出在哪裡。因此，本課程不僅探討美國政治中各種行為者的作為，更進一步分析其背後的原因。課程涵蓋主題包括：1)美國憲法的邏輯與架構；2)公民的態度與行為；3)影響政治選戰的因素及選戰如何影響選舉結果；4)政黨的本質及其如何促進或妨礙民主治理；5)美國國會與總統職權所面臨的兩難；6)美國總統職權為何以及如何日益擴張。
課程目標與學習成效: 美國政治一直是許多政治學理論與實證研究的發源地。本課程的設計旨在提供學生一個宏觀且具系統性的入門導覽，幫助理解美國政治學如何發展出理論架構來解釋政治制度與行為。課程的核心不僅止於介紹美國政治的現況或事實，而是聚焦於學術層面，探討研究者如何運用理論工具分析政治現象。希望修課同學在完成課程後，能將這些理論觀點靈活運用到其他政治學相關議題的研究中。

課程簡介:
中東地區位居歐、亞、非三洲交會之處，不僅是世界主要宗教的發源地，也是全球能源供應、地緣政治競逐與國際安全的重要核心。近年來，阿拉伯之春運動、伊斯蘭國（ISIS）興衰、2023年加薩戰爭，以及美國、中國、伊朗、以色列與阿拉伯國家之間日益複雜的戰略互動，更使中東成為理解當代國際政治不可或缺的重要區域。
本課程旨在介紹中東地區的歷史發展、政治制度、國際關係與安全議題，協助學生建立對中東區域政治的基本認識與分析能力。課程首先回顧近代中東國家體系的形成，並介紹國際關係理論的重要觀點，使學生能運用不同理論分析中東政治的發展脈絡與國際互動。其次，課程將探討美國與中國等域外強權在中東的戰略布局，以及區域國家在大國競逐下所採取的外交與安全策略。
理論基礎建立後，課程進一步聚焦中東當代的重要政治與安全議題，包括：阿以衝突與和平進程、阿拉伯之春運動、阿富汗戰爭、伊拉克戰爭、伊斯蘭國的崛起與衰落、伊朗的區域影響力、卡達的小國外交，以及2023年加薩戰爭與近期美以伊衝突對區域秩序的影響。透過相關案例的分析，學生將深入理解歷史因素、宗教認同、國內政治與國際權力競逐如何共同塑造當代中東的政治發展與安全環境。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程結合國內外重要學術文獻與最新國際時事，鼓勵學生從多元理論視角思考中東問題，培養獨立分析與批判思考能力。課程亦強調歷史脈絡與現實政治的結合，使學生不僅能掌握中東區域的重要議題，更能理解其與全球政治、國際安全及大國競爭之間的密切關聯，進而建立分析當代國際事務所需的基礎知識與能力。

課程簡介:
本課程將介紹美國、日本、法國、德國、英國等國的政府制度，雖然同為民主國家，各國依其採取的不同制度，如總統制、內閣制、半總統制，如何影響其政治發展及治理情況，尤其採取同政治制度亦可能有不同的樣貌。另一方面，本課程亦討論不同國家特殊國情、歷史、政治文化如何影響其政治菁英決定的政治制度；而公民社會、政治文化、政黨政治在不同制度下又呈現何種互動模式？由於所選國家皆為民主（liberal Democratic）國家，本課程亦將討論這些國家的民主化進程。
上課以ＰＰＴ授課為主，課堂討論為輔。課堂中將適度挑選與主題相關的影片，旨在以畫面讓學生感受各國政治及社會情況。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程的主要目標：在學術訓練上，希望能為本校有志從事政治及外交研究的學生，培養對政治制度的基本理解，包括了解政治制度如何影響決策、政治文化、政府與社會關係等。此外，單純就外交研究而言，對於各國的政治制度了解越深入，越能理解各國的外交政策及其決策思維差異，幫助學生增加對於國際事務理解的深度及廣度。在人才培育上，藉由課堂發表及撰寫報告，培養學生統整知識及獨立思考的能力，訓練外交政策分析的基本能力。

本課程旨在闡明各國外交政策的決策過程，探討影響決策方向的若干國際、國內、以及個人因素。課程內容從理性選擇、公共選擇理論出發，建立對於決策科學理論的認識，佐以目前對政府以及企業決策的分析，討論如何能做出完善、符合行為者利益的決策。課程規劃以層次分析為主軸，討論個人、國內、以及國際體系三種層次的因素如何影響政治菁英、決策團體、利益團體、官僚組織、及否決者。本課程期望學生瞭解外交政策制定的過程中，決策者與國內外各式行為者之間的互動關係，洞察外交政策背後各種因素，以理論闡釋各種因素之間的因果關係，培養分析外交政策的書寫與口頭表達能力，最後，學生將學習如何評價外交政策，並且利用理論架構分析外交政策的未來走向。本課程將介紹學界對外交政策之制訂的相關理論以及研究發現，也將討論這些研究的可靠性與實用性。

課程簡介: This course aims to educate students to seize the particular dynamics and political issues within the European Union (EU), and also, its relations with other parts of the world. While the EU has undergone significant political transformation since the second World War, its singular course of integration amidst crises and collective community building provides rich subjects for political studies. By the end of the semester, the students are expected to understand the major players in Europe, the unique governance model of the EU, and the distinctive issues the EU faces. Students are also expected to be able to analyze a given European issue with rightful approaches.
課程目標與學習成效: This course is to survey the international relations of the EU since 1945. It will be divided into three sections. The first part introduces the particular European political culture and the governance model of the EU. The second part looks into the foreign policy of major European actors. The final section will examine the relations between the EU and extra-regional states.

課程簡介:
This course is an overview of international economics, and introduces students to basic concepts, theories, and policies on international economics. The first half of this course is focused on the most important issue in international economics—trade. We will cover a number of well-known trade models and trade policies, and discuss how they are applied to or functioning in the real world. The second half of this course is about international finance and macroeconomics. We will discuss issues such as exchange rates, capital control, financial globalization, and economic crisis. While this course is quite theoretical, we will use real-world examples (such as the Sino-US trade war) to illustrate international economics theories, which hopefully will enhance students’ understanding of how international economics works.
From Week 2 onwards, you will be given homework to work on every week, and are expected to submit your answers to the Moodle by the next class (i.e., 1:10am on Monday). Late submissions will not be accepted.
課程目標與學習成效: Upon completing this course, students are expected to (1) understand the basic concept of trade, (2) be able to tell the differences among three trade models, (3) be aware of the basic concepts of international finance, and (4) understand exchange rates and international monetary systems.

課程簡介: Development is a topic that has fascinated scholars in the social sciences for several decades. In the study of relations between states, and lately incorporating non-state actors, a constant question has been raised: Why some countries develop more than others? What are the elements that can help states and societies to transform and modernize themselves? Multiple answers to those questions have been offered throughout the years. The main goal of this course is to make students more familiar with the different theories and concepts around the decision-making of problems associated with development at the international level. Going beyond the traditional models, which are introduced in the first weeks of the semester, the course also will present students with other topics related to the area of development studies, such as institutions, policies, poverty, inequality, security, and aid, among others.

課程簡介:
With a growing confrontation of Sino-US strategic tit-for-tat and globalization versus de-globalization, the globe has become more complext than ever. As a result,
the world economy has become fragmented and global power landscape
is s
hifting in a big way.
Taught in English,
this course attempts to offer an innovative way to examine current global politics and economy.
It is designed to grant students basic knowledge and analytical tools for the understanding and explanation of the foreign policies in a comparative way. The course begins with the introduction of comparative analysis, including why to compare, what to compare and how to compare. Then, the evolution of comparative analysis approach including main paradigms and models will be explored in depth. Discussion comprises how states formulate and implement their foreign policies in general and why nations act differently. By examining literature on foreign policy it will look into rational state actors, institutional, societal, and psychological models. The course will debate government decision-makers, organizations, political parties, private interests, social groups, and mass public that have an impact on foreign policy. It analyzes the various constraints within which each of these sets of actors must operate, the nature of their interactions with each other and with the society as a whole, and the processes and mechanisms through which they resolve their differences and formulate policy.
課程目標與學習成效:
Course Objectives
:
To help students understand why nations act differently, why different decision makers view outside world differently and why different institutions make policies and implement policies differently. On the other hand, some nations do share similar approaches to dealing with international affairs such as middle power diplomacy, foreign policy of divided nations. To help students make comparison and contrast with vertical comparative analysis and horizontal comparative analysis.
Learning Outcomes
Students will be able to independently explore and analyze a number of real world cases of foreign policy decision making and different foreign policy behavior of countries through the application of comparative studies theories and approaches.
Examination of how and why states develop distinct foreign policies through review of prominent theoretical perspectives in the comparative foreign policy literature.

課程簡介:
社會研究法是社會學的核心課程之一，旨在為學生提供一套完整且嚴謹的社會研究方法，以便深入分析各種社會現象。在這一年的必修課程中，我們將分兩個學期來系統地介紹質性和量化研究方法。
第一學期將重點介紹質性研究方法，課程的核心是方法的操作和實踐。透過實作及各項方法的演練，學生將學習並理解不同質性研究方法背後的知識論假設及其運作邏輯。課程內容包括但不限於：(1)參與觀察：通過參與觀察法，學生將掌握如何在自然環境中收集資料，並理解其行為和現象；(2)深度訪談：學習如何設計訪談問題，進行訪談並系統性地分析訪談資料，以揭示潛在的模式和主題；(3)紮根理論：理解並應用紮根理論來構建理論模型，解釋社會現象。透過這些學習，學生將具備蒐集、處理
和分析不同類型的質性資料，解讀複雜的經驗現象，並能熟練操作各種質性研究方法。
在第一學期掌握了常見的質性研究方法後，第二學期將重點轉向量化研究。我們將進一步培養學生應用所學的研究工具，結合理論與研究設計，將抽象的研究問題轉化為具體的研究步驟，並進行實地資料蒐集與統計分析。最終，學生將完成一個符合社會科學精神和方法的量化經驗研究，並根據研究成果撰寫完整的社會研究報告。
這門課程的設計旨在全面提升學生在社會研究中的理論素養和實踐能力，使其能夠獨立完成從問題設定到資料分析的整個研究過程，為未來的學術研究和實務工作奠定堅實的基礎。
課程目標與學習成效: 在第二學期的課程中，我們除了介紹量化研究方法外，將針對社會研究的主要類型、理論與研究、方法論的意義、回顧文獻和執行倫理研究、研究設計的策略、量化分析應用軟體 R 等進行介紹。這學期每組學生需要完成一份採用量化取徑的研究計畫，且內容須包含文獻探討、研究架構、問卷題目設計、抽樣與問卷調查訪談、問卷資料整理和統計分析、討論和參考書目，並在期末完成研究計畫的執行並繳交研究報告。

課程目的：
本課程「新社會思想史」顧名思義指「新—社會思想史」，是取代「社會思想史」的進階設計，但並不必然需要先備社會思想史的知識。又新社會思想史也意指「新社會—思想史」，是為要理解新興社會現實的基本理念形式。
新社會思想史和社會思想史的傳統課程目的一致，都企圖探討當代社會現實的思想源起和背景，尤其泛指西方或特指歐洲社會脈絡下的理念結構。但是，社會思想史一般多在回溯社會學出現之前的非社會學思想條件，因此通常止於 19 世紀晚期。
而新社會思想史則將持續跟隨社會學門的思想發展，從 19 世紀末建制化到 20 世紀末去建制化的歷程，追蹤同期各種非社會學，但帶有社會學精神的論述表達。課程期望同學們，在經驗當前社會現象時，能夠習得歷史想像、結構觀察、實踐反思的各項能力。

容將並重歷史社會脈絡和經典文本導讀這兩個層次，並且同學們將組成小組挑選
其中一部分經典進行研讀、報告和討論。

大數據
社會分析
是社會學的重要課程之一，旨在為學生提供一套系統性和嚴謹的數據資料分析方法，以便在科技和人工智慧主導社會潮流的時代裡能夠有紮實的能力去深入探討各種社會現象。

課程簡介:
質性研究並不只是一組研究技術。訪談、觀察、民族誌、文本分析與檔案研究之所以能夠成為研究方法，是因為研究者對於「社會世界由什麼構成」、「行動者如何形成意義」、「什麼可以成為研究材料」，以及「研究者如何形成解釋」抱持特定的理論與認識論預設。
過去數十年，人文社會科學對社會世界的理解經歷了一系列重要轉變。從文化、意義與再現，到論述、權力與主體性；從身體、空間與日常生活，到物質性、關係、基礎設施與社會技術系統；近年更隨著平台化、資料化、演算法與生成式人工智慧的發展，使研究者必須重新思考：當社會行動不再能夠單純從人的主觀意義加以理解時，質性研究究竟應該觀察什麼、蒐集什麼，又應如何分析？
本課程以修習過基礎質性研究方法為前提，不再以訪談、觀察、編碼等基本技術為主要內容，而是將
社會與文化理論的轉變，與質性研究方法論的發展並置閱讀
。課程第一部分由文化研究與社會理論出發，理解特定研究問題如何在不同歷史條件與理論典範中形成；第二部分進一步追問，當研究者以不同方式理解社會世界時，研究問題、田野、材料與分析如何隨之改變。因此，本課程所謂「進階」，並不是學習更多方法名稱，而是培養研究者在
理論、研究問題、經驗材料與分析之間往復辯證思考與運用的能力
。
課程目標與學習成效:
理解當代質性研究主要理論與方法論轉向的歷史脈絡。
辨識不同社會／文化理論如何改變研究者對經驗世界的觀看方式。
將抽象理論概念轉化為可研究的問題、場域與經驗材料。
重新檢視訪談、觀察、民族誌、文本與文件等既有方法的認識論預設。
理解物質性、關係、基礎設施、數位平台、演算法與AI對質性研究提出的新問題。
能夠依研究問題整合不同形式的質性材料，而非以單一方法決定研究設計。
培養對研究者位置、詮釋權威、AI協作與研究倫理的反身能力。
最終形成一份具有清楚理論
—
方法關係的研究設計。

課程簡介:
慈善經常被理解為出於善意而幫助他人的道德行為，但從社會學的角度來看，慈善從來不只是「做好事」。誰有能力施予、什麼樣的需求被認定值得援助、善意如何轉化為持續運作的組織，以及私人資源為何能夠介入公共事務，都涉及特定的社會關係、文化價值、制度安排與權力結構。本課程以慈善（charity）與公益慈善（philanthropy）為研究對象，探討施予如何從個人道德行動發展為現代社會中的組織與公共制度，並分析慈善與宗教、非營利組織、福利國家、市場、公民社會、不平等、民主及社會正義之間的複雜關係。
課程以 Rhodri Davies《慈善有什麼用？》為主要教材，循著「什麼是慈善」、「慈善還是救濟」、「慈善還是正義」、「慈善還是國家」、「慈善還是民主」與「慈善還是市場」等問題逐步展開。前半學期首先建立慈善研究的概念、歷史與社會學基礎，並透過中國明清慈善史與宗教慈善的比較，避免將現代英美 philanthropy 視為唯一的慈善發展模式；進而分析善意如何透過非營利組織與宗教信仰為本的組織（FBO）制度化。後半學期則將慈善置入現代政治經濟秩序，追問私人慈善是否補充或取代國家責任、慈善能否處理結構性不平等、富豪與基金會介入公共政策的民主正當性，以及市場化、社會企業與有效利他主義如何重新定義「好的慈善」。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程並不預設慈善必然具有正面效果，也不將批判慈善作為預定結論，而是要求學生在歷史、比較與制度分析的基礎上，辨析慈善可能具有的救濟、公共服務、社會創新與公共善功能，以及伴隨而來的分配、權力與問責問題。學期最後將回到全課的核心提問：在什麼社會與制度條件下，私人施予可以成為具有公共正當性的慈善行動？慈善究竟應該做什麼，又有哪些事情不應由慈善取代？

以Dominic Strinati所著的《概述通俗文化理論》(2009)一書為主，介紹齊美爾、法蘭克福學派、結構與後結構主義、符號學等各體系的大眾文化理論。

選課設定_限制與加簽: 開放低年級: 是 Yes｜非本院名額: 10｜總名額: 10｜開放加簽: 否 No
115-1課表備註: 彭保羅教授先前開設之「蓋婭政治、生態與戰爭」課程與此課程內容有部分相似，但課程整體上會有相當不同，比較強調社運和國內政治的角色，以前修過彭老師課程的同學若有興趣歡迎再次選修。
課程簡介:
The notion of Gaia-politics challenges traditional approaches to sovereignty by taking more seriously the geo of geopolitics, that is to say its environmental dimension. War ecology is another concept that aims to address the concomitance of the climate emergency with more traditional threats on national security including military and civilian defense. Through guess lectures, off campus visits and negotiation theaters, the class focuses on the case of Taiwan in comparison with other countries.
In 2023, this course focused on conflicts between humans and non-humans. In 2024, we paid attention to the role of social movements (such as environmental protection and antinuclear mobilization), and how they connect with national politics, in particular state agencies and the parliament. In 2025, we explored with a critical eye the catchwords of ‘social resilience’, ‘technological innovation’ and ‘energy transition’, and how these effectively influence collective preparation to climate change and war scenarios.
In 2026, while continuing our research on these topics, we will also conduct an educational experiment that requires us to spend most of our time out of the classroom. The idea is to take a pause, detox from our overuse of electronics and AI, and return to the basics of ethnographic fieldwork with our eyes and ears wide open, using handwritten notes and drawings.
「蓋婭政治」(Gaia-politics)的概念挑戰了「主權」 概念的傳統取徑，因為蓋婭政治更認真看待「地緣政治」中的「地緣」，也就是其環境面向。「戰爭生態學」(war ecology)則是另一個概念，旨在面對氣候緊急狀態與傳統國安威脅(包括軍事與民間防 衛)共存的局勢。
透過客座課程、校外參訪與協商劇場的形式，本課 程將聚焦於台灣相較於其他國家的情勢。2023年， 本課程聚焦於人類與非人類之間的衝突。2024年， 我們更注重社會運動(如環保與反核運動)的角 色，以及它們如何與國內政治——特別是政府機構與國會——產生連結。
2025年，我們將在延續對跨物種正義、社會運動與 國家政治的關注之餘，進一步批判性地探討「社會 韌性」、「科技創新」與「能源轉型」這些關鍵詞，並檢視它們如何實質地影響集體面對氣候變遷與戰爭 情境的準備與應對能力。
2026年，我們除了將繼續探索上述議題，亦會將多數時間移至教室之外，進行一項教育性實驗計畫。本計畫旨在按下暫停鍵，戒斷我們對3C產品與人工智慧的過度使用；並以敏銳的觀察與傾聽，透過手寫與手繪紀錄，回歸民族誌田野工作的基礎。
課程目標與學習成效:
The goal of this mixed-method approach—using ethnographic fieldwork and negotiation theater—is to improve our capacity to detach from electronic devices and increase our focus while reading scientific papers, attending lectures, participating in group discussions, and conducting ethnographic fieldwork. In other words, this means listening and observing, taking valuable notes, and turning these observations into social capital and political will through class discussions. Meanwhile, protests against the environmental cost of electronic waste and the huge carbon footprint of AI data centers provide further reminders and incentives to detox from electronics. Last but not least, as Taiwan’s civil defense organizations train their members, we must also learn to cope with electricity shortages or blackouts in the event of a military emergency, natural hazard, or industrial disaster (such as earthquakes, typhoons, or gas explosions).
課程目標與預期成果：本課程透過民族誌田野工作與協商劇場的混合途徑，旨在幫助我們降低對電子產品的依賴，藉此提升在閱讀文獻、參與講座、小組討論與田野工作時的專注力。具體而言，我們將練習觀察與傾聽、作好筆記，並透過課堂討論將這些觀察轉化為社會資本與政治動能。此外，遠離 3C 也是對當前社會與環境議題的反思。電子垃圾的環境代價與 AI 資料中心的巨大碳足跡，不斷提醒並促使我們減少對電子設備的依賴。最後，正如台灣民防組織對其會員的訓練，我們也必須透過這門課學會：在遭遇軍事衝突或天災人禍（如地震、颱風、氣爆）時，如何面對並適應缺電或停電的狀態。

課程簡介:
This course introduces students to the sociological study of technoscience and society. You will explore and analyze what it means to live in a contemporary technological society. A major goal will be to answer several questions: (1) What are the social, structural, and cultural influences on our behavior, attitudes, and technological change? (2) What are the sources, dynamics, and consequences of social inequality and of how we are organized? (3) What are the implications of materials and technology for social change? We will then discuss fundamental social processes and concepts—culture, organization and management, social identity, and social interaction.
In the later part of the semester, you will study how technology and society have been intertwined. While technology has always been an intricate part of any society, in the second half of the 20th-century technological change became a defining characteristic of the way societal structures, and technological politics are constituted and organized. In this part, you will investigate and unravel this distinctive condition. You will study different areas where questions about technology’s role in society are central: economy, transportation, and corporations. 課程簡介:
Today’s world is becoming more interconnected and globalized. Public health issues — such as infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and emerging technologies — are no longer national or regional problems; they are increasingly addressed through a global, integrated, and multidisciplinary approach.
This course empowers students, future policy-makers, and practitioners to analyze and engage with global health issues. Each week introduces a topic in global health governance — such as the World Health Organization and the International Health Regulations, pandemic preparedness, climate change and human health, health technology and digital health, health financing, and One Health — led by the instructors or invited guest speakers. Reflecting recent World Health Assembly priorities, the 2026 edition gives expanded attention to climate change and human health, health technology, and the financing of global health.
In the final weeks, the class executes a simulated public health emergency under the World Health Organization framework (the WHO Simulation), joined by outside experts, civil society, and journalists. Students are divided into four to five countries and assigned roles as key legal, policy, and public health decision-makers responding to the scenario. The simulation consolidates what students learn across the term and builds their competencies in global health governance.

•  Develop the ability to participate in international conferences, deliver oral presentations, and collaborate in teams.
•  Build research capabilities using media, literature, and databases, and gain front-line experience of health policy-making through the WHO Simulation.
•  Broaden horizons beyond students’ own disciplines, deepening understanding of public health, biomedicine, law, and international relations.

課程簡介:
本課程不開放加簽！
（此課程大綱
為暫訂版，以開學後的版本為準
）
自十九世紀中葉開始，隨著工業化和都市化的累積發展，文化出現了顯著的變異。社會生活節奏加速，人們相信唯有「變動」才是恆常不變的現象，也將變動視為進步的象徵。如同波特萊爾筆下對現代性的洞察，十九世紀末、二十世紀初的藝術領域面對劇烈的社會變遷，加上藝術內部的自我反思與革新實驗，啟動了重新界定藝術的動力。無論是音樂、舞蹈、小說、戲劇、詩、繪畫與建築，現代主義藝術紛紛揚棄傳統的典範，開啟一場「永恆的革命」------英國藝術史學家E.Gombrich的用語，其中又以視覺藝術的表現最為激烈。
美國藝評家C. Greenberg在〈現代主義繪畫〉(1961) 提及，現代主義藝術始於「自我批判」，每種範疇的藝術皆要求以獨一無二、不可替代的方法，展現自身本來的面目、提供獨特的藝術經驗。在追求「純粹性」的方向中，找到自己的質量與獨立的標準。提煉純粹性的同時也顛覆了藝術昔日的定義。藝術並非藉由他律而存有，更無法被其他藝術類型取代、被其他社會文化干預。Greenberg提出繪畫的幾項基本構成要素，包括：平面性(flatness of surface)、封閉的形狀或框架(enclosing shape of picture or frame)，以及顏料的質感(paint texture)等等，其中又以「平面性」專屬繪畫藝術所有。上述這些繪畫的特性，成為現代主義畫作強調的重點。然而，Greenberg的論點，似乎將現代主義的繪畫導向一種忽視社會與政治影響力的「形式主義」。
縱然現代主義藝術在形式上的強調前所未有，不過以藝術社會學的取徑觀之，藝術家仍舊是社會的一員，並且對於社會生活有著不等程度的融入。即使藝術成為一種反叛與革命的形式，此一對抗性實則突顯出藝術與社會的互動關連，如同孤獨本身極具社會意涵一般。除了觸及藝術作品的藝術性與美學面向之外，本課程將格外看重現代藝術發展的社會條件與文化精神------並非將美學以外的因素僅僅視為藝術的外部條件，亦非把創作的歷史發展看作藝術的疏離背景，而是整體性地辯證：現代主義藝術追求的自主性與革命性如何可能？
就探討的藝術範疇而言，鑑於視覺藝術在西方現代主義的活躍性，課程將以繪畫領域為主，雕塑為輔，並聚焦於繪畫本身二維向度的基進回歸與嶄新突破。如同每一種藝術流派的考察一樣，現代主義藝術的起迄時間向來難以定於一尊。若以藝術史上風格的根本轉變作為劃分標準、考慮學期週數所限，從印象派之前的馬內(Manet)開始，到戰後抽象表現主義為止，大致上是一種保守而周全的分野，研究時也應該對任何藝術本質的定義與歷史分期方法採取開放的態度。
就研討主題而論，固然現代主義藝術如同春秋戰國時代的百家爭鳴，藝術史學家與評論者對於這一段歷史各有其申論之重點，例如形式主義與政治實踐的不同強調，但作為與傳統藝術作品有別的對照面，現代主義即使無法全然與過往歷史脫離，仍可掌握其不同於古典藝術的特徵與傾向，包括藝術的自我批判、重新定義、實驗性格與自主性的追求。
現代主義藝術主體性的指涉至少包含三個面向：一、藝術家作為個人的主體性; 二、藝術家作為獨立藝術家的主體性; 三、藝術及藝術場域作為自主領域的主體性。若納入藝術創作者以外的行動者，藝術的主體性尚可包括藝術史學家歷史觀點的主觀性，以及藝術評論者批評藝術家及作品時抱持的主觀性。藝術的宗旨自此傾向尋求主觀化與表現性，取代古典藝術再現真理與體現「美」的使命。我們將透過解析與鑑賞各個流派的藝術品，針對藝術的現代性累積出心得。如同現代主義藝術一般，本課程期望透過自我詰問的過程，再次對藝術、對自身進行審視。現代主義自我批判與實驗精神所帶來的啟發，亦能引導當代的個體重新內觀自身時下的存在。
為了對於現代藝術史的發展具備基礎的瞭解，邵大箴主編的《西方美術欣賞》與E.H.Gombrich的經典《藝術的故事》，將成為本課程藝術史的基礎材料，佐以英國藝術史學家與哲學家Herbert Read (1893-1968)所著的
A Concise History of Modern Painting
(現代繪畫史)作為教材。前者清楚提供藝術簡史，後兩位則聚焦於特殊史觀的學術闡述。即使各個作者難免依照主觀意見，將某些藝術家與畫派納入或排除於著作之外，但是藝術史本身具備的歷史觀點本為學術考究的對象。選修這門課的同學應養成獨立學習之興趣，主動延伸閱讀相關藝術史文獻。
鑑於學界少見符合本科目旨趣的既定書目，因此課程大綱所條列的讀本及參考書目，主要是為了幫助學生建立相關知識基礎，教師將從多元文獻中整理製作PPT及講綱。學生因此務必出席每堂課程、參與討論。
課程目標與學習成效:
1.建立以人文社會科學進行視覺藝術研究的專業基礎
2.訓練以社會學及藝術史學分析視覺形式與圖像意義的技巧
3.培養美學及關懷社會文化的素養
4.具備製作獨立藝術社會學專題報告的能力

科目名稱: 反身社會學經典研讀：Garfinkel俗民方法學
英文科目名稱: Classics of Reflexive Sociology: Garfinkel's Ethnomethodolog y

課程簡介:
法國社會學家P. Bourdieu主張，讓當代社會學與古典社會學區分開來的重要特色在於反身性（reflexivity）。亦即，相較於古典社會學急於瞭解其當下的現代社會與過去的傳統社會之差異，當代社會學則注意到，古典社會學對其當下社會的反省，往往也指向了支撐起古典社會學自身的基礎，例如科學、理性等等。換言之，如果批判資本主義政治經濟體制的可能性，也是建立在讓資本主義得以運行的機能，那麼這樣的批判與所指出的出路是徹底的而可能實現的嗎？還是僅僅是資本主義政治經濟體制的自我療癒。
同理，社會學家也是社會成員之一，其對社會人的描繪也適用於社會學家自身。當社會學家分析關係網絡、權力、利益、或階級與成長過程對個人的影響時，也該注意到這些因素亦可能影響社會學家的研究而造成研究上的盲點。進而，當社會學家認為一般人日常生活中的認知判斷是以理所當然為其不可或缺的基礎，那麼學者在其日常的學術研究中亦是如此。這樣的自覺當然也拉下了學者、尤其是社會學家高高在上，且自以為是的客觀超然地位。
美國社會學家H. Garfinkel早在Bourdieu之前就已經提出反身性的概念。並據此別開生面地結合了社會現象學的理論觀點與他自己所開創的經驗研究。其研究涵蓋了一般人的日常生活與學者的學術研究。甚至也影響了Woolgar與Latour合著的《實驗室生活》，其重要性與開創性可見一斑。但其著作也堪稱社會學的天書之一。不只其論述思想因反身性而變得纏繞複雜，其行文構句亦隨之冗長難解。因此，我們將這學期的課程帶領修課同學直接進入其原典，藉以培養學生自主閱讀與思辨的能力。
課程目標與學習成效: 我們將這學期的課程帶領修課同學直接進入其原典，藉以培養學生自主閱讀與思辨的能力。

This is an undergraduate course in the sociology of education. As higher education becomes more globalized, students learn to become global citizens not only through their schooling experiences but also through their mobility trajectories. In this course, we will collectively explore questions that emerge from your day-to-day educational experiences. For example, how do different educational systems operate, and how are students from different systems different from or similar to one another? Who can study abroad, and are education and college admissions fair to all?
In this course, we will read literature in sociology of education that examines
educational structures and schooling experiences in various countries, focusing on inequality in educational systems. We will first learn about the overall themes such as schooling, school organization, family and school, and higher education. Thereafter, we will turn to examples that include the U.S., U.K., France, the Netherlands, Ireland, Taiwan, China, and South Korea to compare and draw on these experiences. I expect students to read the literature and examine and share examples that provide comparative insights from their own experiences. To this end, this course seeks to provide a holistic picture of global society without losing sight of the contextual specificities that shape both individual and class-based experiences in the schooling process.
課程目標與學習成效:
Learning Outcomes
Explain central concepts in the sociology of education in clear, non-technical English.
Use sociological concepts to interpret personal and observed educational experiences without treating one experience as universal.
Compare how schools, families, higher education, and labor markets produce opportunities and inequalities.
Distinguish claims, evidence, and methods in accessible empirical research.
Develop and defend an evidence-based interpretation in an oral report and respond constructively to questions.

在經濟學中，數理方法是不可或缺的工具，被廣泛地應用於經濟理論的證明與推導中。除此之外，資訊工具在經濟分析中扮演著日漸重要的角色。然而對於數學和資訊工具的不熟悉，常是同學在學習公共經濟議題分析時的挫折來源。本課程因此希望能幫助對於經濟分析有興趣的學生，介紹在此領域中常用的基礎數學與資訊工具，透過課堂講授與課後練習，逐步培養學生將數理方法應用於經濟問題分析的能力。

課程簡介:
（學校網頁教學大綱依學校既定格式填寫，實際課程進行按本課程網頁課綱及公告。）
《租稅法》為財政系大學部四年級唯一各組必修之課程，是許多國家考試之指定科目，其重要性可見。就財政系核心課程之架構而言，經過了一年級經濟原理及初級會計的紮根、二年級經濟學理論的進一步探討與財政學理論的導讀以及三年級租稅各稅的討論，在四年級的《租稅法》課程的要求，應結合前三年級所學，細膩的剖析我國稅制。
然長久以來，同學對於《租稅法》課程往往有「繁雜」及「瑣碎」之印象。不諱言，十數種稅目一一走過，不論修習過、正在修習或準備修習此一科目的同學，甚至於對教授此一課程的講師，都很難避免上述之感受。因此，在一開始必須要有一定的心理準備，以一致的邏輯性、有系統的來討論各種稅制。就財政系的學生而言，此邏輯性必然的為財政學最根本的公平與效率。
在滿足一既定之稅收的要求的大前提下，租稅的存在勢必對分配─所得、消費、及財富─的公平面以及資源配置的效率面造成一定的衝擊。以公平的面相來看租稅，討論的課題在於：稅制之設計及修改如何影響分配的公平性。以效率的面向來看租稅，討論的課題則在於：稅制之設計及修改如何減輕其對資源配置的負面影響。換言之，由於租稅具有公平及效率之兩大功能性，就「租稅規劃」而言，在滿足政府一定財政需求的前提下，理當設計一既能改善分配的情況、又能促進整體資源使用效率之稅制。然而問題在於，不論就理論及實務而言，由於公平及效率兩大目標之相互牴觸，此一理想之稅制皆不存在。
本課程著重於以公平的面相來探討我國之稅制，主要理由如下:
鮮（沒）有租稅的存在的根本目的在促進整體經濟資源使用的效率。既然租稅的存在對整體經濟效率的負面影響不可避免，何不細問究竟此一代價能否成就分配的公平性。
就資源使用的效率面而言，在其他條件相同或不變的情形下，租稅制度或許有其邊際的效果。然而其他條件往往不同，其他條件也往往會變，而租稅制度在資源使用的決策而言也非必然扮演邊際考量的角色。試問有誰因為所得稅的課徵而選擇失業，以不賺取所得來規避稅負?
當下所得、消費以及財富分配的情形每下愈況，已成為嚴重的社會問題。選擇以公平的面相來探討我國之稅制，也有身為財政人「贖罪」的犬儒心態。
最後，《租稅法》向來為上下學期各2學分、共計4學分的安排。時間的限制下，既使全力以赴，學年間課程之進行，一旦因國定假日或其他原因停課，勢必無法完成預計的進度。又，稅制不斷演進，課堂的討論，如閉門造車而不能將進行中的稅改討論帶入，意義何在？但上下學期各2學分、共計4學分的安排，往往造成稅改討論與課程進度，此顧彼失的情形。本人2011年擔任《租稅法》課程講師以來，不斷爭取將《租稅法》改為上下學期各3學分、共計6學分的安排；怎奈此與學校降低必修學分數、精簡課程的大方向相違。在形勢比人強的情形下，只得退而求其次，將《租稅法》課程切割為二、改為《租稅法（一）》與《租稅法（二）》兩門單學期各3學分的安排。對於財政學系稅務組同學而言，由於兩門課程皆為必修，相當於多了2學分的租稅法課程，達成上下學期各3學分、共計6學分的目的。對於財政學系非稅務組與非財政學系主修的學生而言，必須理解《租稅法（一）》與《租稅法（二）》，為連貫的課程設計，修習上學期的《租稅法（一）》，僅有完整課程一半的內容，著重於所得稅的探討，並沒有涵蓋財產與消費稅的討論（參見授課進度）。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程的目標在帶領修習者就各種租稅制度進行深入的探討，期能對我國現行稅制有完整的認識。

課程採每週影片自學結合實體課堂之混合式教學模式：學生須於課前自主觀看當週教材影片，於實體課堂中再由授課教師進行重點複習，並透過結構化之合作學習活動深化理解與記憶，最後以隨堂測驗檢核學習成效（詳見「每週學習方式」與「教學方法」二節）。課程亦包含分組課堂報告以強化學習成果，並於學年課程結束後，另行安排跨校交流活動，邀請表現優異學生組隊參與專題報告競賽，由業界主管進行評審與回饋，藉此增進學生與業界之互動與連結；此活動與課程進度表中各週次之「專題演講」為不同性質之安排，前者為學期外之跨校競賽活動，後者為課堂內之邀請講者演講。
本課程對應之基本素養：透過分析總體經濟、國際市場趨勢及各類金融商品應用，培養學生對全球資產管理市場之專業理解與國際視野，提升其於多元文化與跨境資本流動環境中之決策與溝通能力；同時，課程涵蓋風險識別與法令遵循，強調誠信經營與合規精神，培育學生之職業倫理意識與金融責任感。課程亦引導學生思考資產管理於社會責任與人文關懷上的角色，透過保險與信託等工具之應用，探討財富傳承與社會公平之實踐，鼓勵學生於追求財務績效之餘，兼顧個人、家庭與社會福祉之平衡。結合業界實務導師之課程設計，協助學生有效銜接職場，成為兼具理論素養、實戰能力與社會責任感之資產管理新秀。
本課程無先修或先備條件，課程設計係針對尚不具資產管理相關基礎之學生。上、下兩學期修畢且成績及格者，由臺灣金融研訓院頒發證書。

課程簡介:
“Mechanism design” is a branch of economics where we are in the shoes of a policy maker, or better yet, a game maker. Traditional game theory takes the rules as given and predicts how players would act. A mechanism designer, however, reverses this process. The designer engineers the rules of a game so that agents will act in a certain way. Hence, mechanism design is also commonly referred to as reverse game theory. In this course, we will focus on how to apply mechanism design to a variety of public policies.
For example, when designing a democratic voting system, the ideal goal is for citizens to “truthfully” vote for their favorite candidate. However, we shall learn it is hard to design such a system when there are three or more candidates (Gibbard-Satterthwaite Theorem). Another example is a two-sided trade. Imagine an agent owns an item and another agent would potentially want to buy it. We shall learn that it is hard to ensure a trade happens without monetarily incentivizing one of the parties (Myerson-Satterthwaite Theorem).
This course can be split into three core pillars:
Chapters 1 and 2: we introduce the formal structures of how individuals make choices and the basics of mechanism design.
Chapters 3 through 5: we discuss topics where a policy or an allocation is determined based on people’s preferences, and how to design rules so people don’t ‘misrepresent’ (or
lie about
) themselves.
Chapters 6 through 9: we bring monetary transfers into the equation, as well as situations where “beliefs” of the private information of others can dictate their behavior (Bayesian-Nash Equilibria).
Note: it is encouraged for students to have taken the second semester of Microeconomics (or a similar course where Game Theory is taught as part of the curriculum) before enrolling in this course. This course is conducted entirely in English. All lectures, course materials, assignments, exams, and presentations will be strictly in English.
課程目標與學習成效:
After this course, a typical student should be able to …
Interpret choice data and detect possible behavioral patterns that violate “rationality”,
Explain key terms in mechanism design and apply them to public policies,
Compare and contrast various voting systems and their shortcomings,
Execute various matching algorithms and their outcomes,
Analyze the role of monetary transfers in auctions and trade,
Illustrate the importance of “beliefs” in a world of incomplete information.

ESG 選擇、實施與治理合規對比
This course aims to lead students into a deep exploration of the core values of
Social Responsibility (S) and Corporate Governance (G) within the ESG framework, while critically benchmarking key environmental (E) performance indicators
. The curriculum systematically covers the structural impact of the net-zero transition on corporate operations, operational standards for social sustainability, and best practices for implementing corporate governance across distinct industry environments. Special emphasis will be placed on
Social Responsibility (such as international human rights, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion [DEI], and employee family-care benefits) and Corporate Governance (including legal compliance, supply chain governance, and tax transparency)

Environmental (E) Commitment and Execution:

water stewardship and net-zero carbon emission commitments
across various industries, and critically track their latest
implementation progress
.

International Human Rights
standards, implement
DEI
policies—specifically focusing on
family-care mechanisms (e.g., parental leave, maternity/paternity leave, and family support)

Compliance

Supply Chain Governance
and corporate tax transparency.
Through domestic and international case studies of both success and failure, expert forum debates, and quantitative/qualitative analysis of sustainability reports, students will learn to objectively evaluate corporate sustainability performance and propose forward-looking strategies and policy recommendations for practical challenges.

課程目標與學習成效:
Learning Objectives and Outcomes
Objectives
Mastering Transition and Governance:
Comprehend the impacts of net-zero transitions and water scarcity on corporate operations, and master the best practices of social responsibility, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance.
Connecting Social Strategy with Performance:
Deeply explore the practical execution of social responsibility (particularly international human rights, family care, and DEI) and its long-term impact on corporate reputation, talent attraction, and financial/fiscal health.
Advanced Sustainability Report Deconstruction:
Cultivate the ability to independently read and critically analyze quantitative E, S, and G metrics and implementation timelines within the sustainability reports of tech, textile, and luxury retail sectors.
Strategic Proposal and Critical Thinking:
Develop problem-solving capabilities to combine fiscal tools and organizational strategy to formulate concrete, actionable solutions for corporate governance deficiencies and supply chain vulnerabilities.
Outcomes
Critical Evaluation of Cross-Industry Sustainability Strategies
Students will be able to independently read, deconstruct, and critically analyze the English sustainability reports of multinational corporations across tech, traditional manufacturing, and luxury retail sectors. They will develop the practical capacity to precisely evaluate actual implementation progress against environmental (E) commitments (e.g., water stewardship and net-zero targets) and effectively identify potential greenwashing practices.
Strategic Planning for Social Responsibility and Inclusive Governance
Students will be able to proficiently apply international human rights and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) frameworks to deeply dissect the variations in employee welfare and family-care strategies across diverse industries. They will acquire the skills to formulate forward-looking strategic plans and actionable solutions for multinational organizations aiming to protect labor rights and optimize work-life balance
Audit and Assessment of Corporate Governance, Legal Compliance, and Supply Chain Management Risks:
Integrating finance and business strategy perspectives, students will be able to systematically evaluate a corporation's compliance thresholds, tax transparency performance, and the execution of its global supply chain governance. They will be equipped to accurately identify and assess potential fiscal risks and reputational damages arising from governance failures or regulatory non-compliance.

課程簡介:
行政法不但是法律學系重要的基礎學科，更是政治學系學生的重要進階法學訓練課程。行政法並非單獨法典，而是由不同的行政相關法典、大法官會議解釋、行政法院判例及行政機關發布之行政命令或函示所構成。其中，在法律層級，更包括與一般人民權利密切相關之行政程序法、行政執行法和行政罰法，以及人民權利受行政機關違法行政處分侵害時，可尋求救濟之行政訴訟法、訴願法。至於與公務人員權益相關者，還包括公務人員服務法、公務人員任用法、公務人員退休法和公務人員行政中立法等。為幫助學生有效學習行政法，本課程將跨越純法學層次對行政法的探討，整合公共行政領域之政治制度與公法等研究範疇，以理論與實務案例並重的授課方式，讓修課之政治學系學生快速領會行政法之體系架構、重要理論與實用範圍。
本課程為全學年課程。第一學期先以引導學生建立行政法基礎概念為主，從法源、一般原則到各類行政行為（行政處分、行政契約等）之合法性控制；第二學期則進一步探討行政制裁（行政罰）、強制執行、公務員法制，以及人民權利受侵害時之救濟途徑（訴願、行政訴訟）與國家責任（國家賠償），期能培養學生完整處理行政法律問題之能力。為此，本課程將跨越純法學層次對行政法的探討，整合公共行政領域之行政制度與公法等研究範疇，以理論與實務案例並重的授課方式，讓修課之公共行政學系學生快速領會行政法之體系架構、重要理論與實用範圍。
課程目標與學習成效:
一、課程目標
(Course Objectives)
課程進行將以清楚易懂之方式，幫助學生系統性的學習及建構行政法學的知識體系，強調「基礎理論」與「實務應用」並重，故有以下具體目標：
（一）建構完整體系
引導學生從憲法基礎出發，融會貫通行政法之原理原則、行政作用、行政救濟等核心領域，建立見樹又見林的法律思維
。
（二）培養實戰能力
透過案例分析，培養學生在面對公務生活、職場工作或國家考試時，具備精準的法律問題意識與解決問題之能力
。
（三）提升學習興趣
以深入淺出的講授方式，降低法學入門門檻，讓非法律系背景同學也能領略行政法學的邏輯之美與實用價值，進而產生學習樂趣
。
二、學習成效
(Student Learning Outcomes)
（一）專業知識掌握
修課學生將有系統地建構行政法學的完整體系。透過本課程，學生不僅能理解「依法行政」、「比例原則」及「信賴保護」等重要原理原則，亦能清楚區辨行政處分、行政契約、法規命令等各類行政行為的法律性質與構成要件。同時，學生亦須學習《行政程序法》、《行政罰法》、《行政執行法》及行政救濟制度的主要規範內容，進而掌握行政法之理論基礎。
（二）實務應用能力
課程設計著重培養學生解決具體法律爭點之實用能力，透過指標性判決與實例演練，學生將學會運用「涵攝」技術，將抽象的法律規範適用於複雜的行政爭議個案（例如公務員懲戒、違建拆除等）。不僅能提升學生在未來公務職涯中識別法律風險與依法行政之能力，亦能強化其在國家考試申論題中建立層次分明、論證嚴謹的答題技巧
。
（三）價值判斷與人文關懷
課程進行中，將引導學生反思在法治國（
Rechtsstaat
）原則下，行政權力行使與人民基本權利保障之間的動態平衡，培養對公共事務的敏銳度。學生將不只停留在法規的字面解釋，更能從合法性與正當性的雙重維度，對重大行政決策或社會議題進行批判性思考，具備身為公共行政專業人才應有的社會關懷與價值視野

課程簡介:
本課程旨在引導學生全面了解公共預算與財政的基本概念、制度與相關議題，並深入探討政府財務行政管理的過程及其實務應用。課程內容涵蓋公共預算的意義、編製、審議與執行等流程，探討政府在財政上的角色與功能、成本效益分析及租稅制度。透過教學講義、即時資料查詢、問題導向學習、分組報告與遊戲化教學等多元方法，提升學生批判思考、解決問題與實務操作能力，使其在未來能具備分析與理解公共預算與財政事務的能力。
This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the basic concepts, systems, and related issues of public budgeting and finance, with a focus on both theoretical knowledge and practical applications. It covers the meaning, preparation, review, and implementation of public budgets, the roles and functions of government in finance, cost-benefit analysis, and the tax system. Through diverse teaching methods—such as lecture notes, real-time data inquiries, problem-based learning, group presentations, and gamification—students will enhance their critical thinking, problem-solving, and practical skills, preparing them to effectively analyze and interpret public budgeting and financial affairs in their future careers or academic pursuits.

建立學生對公共預算與財政之核心概念及制度架構的理解。
培養學生分析政府財務運作及政策影響的能力。
增進學生應用成本效益分析與財政評估工具的能力。
養成學生批判性思考與解決公共財政問題的能力。
提升學生在公共預算與財政領域的實務操作與溝通表達能力。

修畢本課程後，學生應能：
說明公共預算與財政的基本概念、流程與制度。
分析並評估政府財務政策與預算編製的影響。
運用成本效益分析等方法，提出具可行性的財政建議。
透過分組討論與報告，展現協作與口頭表達能力。
具備解讀財務數據與理解財政決策背景的能力。
Course Objectives
To develop students’ understanding of the core concepts and institutional frameworks of public budgeting and finance.
To equip students with the ability to analyze government financial operations and policy impacts.
To enhance students’ capacity to apply cost-benefit analysis and fiscal assessment tools.
To cultivate critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the field of public finance.
To improve practical skills and communication abilities related to public budgeting and finance.
Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
Explain the fundamental concepts, processes, and systems of public budgeting and finance.
Analyze and evaluate the impacts of government fiscal policies and budget preparation.
Apply methods such as cost-benefit analysis to provide feasible fiscal recommendations.
Demonstrate teamwork and oral communication skills through group discussions and presentations.
Interpret financial data and understand the context of fiscal decision-making.

課程簡介:
「第三部門」是什麼？日常生活中常見的非營利組織、非政府組織、公益與慈善組織、志願服務組織、公民社會組織、草根組織與社會服務組織，伴隨民主化而興起，對政府治理與公民社會發展扮演關鍵角色。
本課程介紹非營利組織與公民社會的概念與理論，分析其角色與功能，探討非營利組織、政府與企業之間的關係，並進一步聚焦於社會創新（social innovation）與社會企業如何回應當代公共議題，包括社區營造、環境與永續轉型，以及跨國的政策移轉與比較治理。

應用理論架構，評估社會需求、組織動態與創新模式。
透過台灣、中國大陸與香港的比較，認識不同政治社會脈絡下公民社會的發展路徑與差異。

課程簡介:
I. Course Objectives
This course is designed to help students understand the legal and governance issues arising from the development of digital technologies, with data governance as its central focus. It addresses major emerging topics, including personal data protection, artificial intelligence governance, digital platform accountability, open government data, data sharing, cybersecurity, cross-border data flows, and the European Union(EU)’s data governance framework.
Taught entirely in English, the course introduces students to core concepts in contemporary international technology law. It examines legal issues that arise throughout the data life cycle, from collection, processing, use, retention, and sharing to deletion. The course also considers the legality of artificial intelligence systems in model training and content generation, and analyzes the respective responsibilities and obligations of governments, businesses, digital platforms, and data intermediaries in data governance.
The course further incorporates Taiwan’s legal framework, the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Data Governance Act, Data Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, and other significant legislative developments and international trends. Through this comparative approach, students will develop a stronger interest in technology law and acquire the analytical skills needed to address practical legal issues.
II. Course Description
This course begins with legal issues related to data use as an entry point into technology law. It introduces key legal concepts, including personal data protection, informational self-determination, privacy, and data governance, before moving to issues such as open government data, data sharing, data intermediary services, data altruism, data access for Internet of Things devices and connected products, cloud switching, regulation of artificial intelligence technologies, algorithmic transparency, disclosure obligations, and legal requirements for cross-border data transfers.
The course focuses on recent developments in the EU’s data governance regime and explains how the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act together shape a technology law framework grounded in trustworthiness, data access, and risk management. In addition to introducing major international technology laws, the course includes weekly case discussions to help students examine the relationship between data governance, personal data protection, public interest, industrial innovation, digital market competition, national data sovereignty, and the protection of fundamental rights.
課程目標與學習成效:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the foundational theories and regulatory structure of technology law and data governance.
Examine legal issues concerning personal data protection, data sharing, digital platform regulation, risk-based regulation of artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity safeguards.
Compare Taiwan’s digital legal framework with the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and other major technology laws of the EU.
Assess, from legal and governance perspectives, personal data protection risks and appropriate levels of regulatory oversight arising from artificial intelligence and other technological applications.
Analyze current disputes and cases involving the application of technology law from an independent perspective and propose appropriate legal or policy reforms.

英文科目名稱: Governing China: Political Change, Social Transformation, and Relations with Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau
選課設定_限制與加簽: 開放低年級: 否 No｜非本院名額: 15｜總名額: 15｜開放加簽: 否 No
課程簡介:
This course examines the rise of China as the defining force shaping politics and society across the Greater China region. Over the past four decades, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has transformed from a poor, isolated polity into the world’s second-largest economy and a leading geopolitical power — with profound consequences not only for its own governance but for its relationship with Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, three societies bound to the mainland by deep cultural and historical ties yet possessing distinct institutional inheritances. The course asks: how has China’s rise reshaped the political institutions, social fabric, and external relationships of each of these polities, and what does the resulting variation tell us about the reach and the limits of Chinese-style governance?
The first half of the course maps the mainland system that drives these dynamics: major theoretical traditions for understanding Chinese politics (authoritarian resilience, fragmented and consultative authoritarianism, adaptive governance, party-state institutionalism); the organisation, ideology, and cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) under Xi Jinping; political change and policy implementation under the post-2012 leadership; the social transformation generated by urbanisation, hukou reform, demographic change, and growing inequality; and state–society relations including civil society, religion, ethnic politics, surveillance, and platform politics.
The second half traces how the rise of China has reshaped — and is being reshaped by — its peripheries. In Hong Kong, the asymmetric integration of the Special Administrative Region into the mainland’s political and economic order has accelerated since 2014, culminating in the 2020 National Security Law, the 2021 “patriots-only” electoral overhaul, and the 2024 Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (Article 23). In Macau, the rise of China has been managed through a quieter politics of accommodation, with deepening integration into the Greater Bay Area and continued reliance on a gaming economy increasingly aligned with Beijing’s strategic priorities. In Taiwan, China’s rise has driven both deepening economic interdependence (trade, investment, ECFA, semiconductors) and an intensifying security competition, with democratisation, identity politics, the 2024 presidential election, and the role of the United States all shaping the cross-Strait equation. The final two weeks are reserved for student case presentations.
課程目標與學習成效: By the end of the course, students should be able to: (1) compare leading theoretical models of Chinese governance and assess their analytical reach; (2) explain how the CCP organises power and recruits, monitors, and disciplines cadres; (3) trace the principal directions of political change under Xi Jinping; (4) analyse social transformation and state–society contention in mainland China; (5) compare the post-handover political trajectories of Hong Kong and Macau; (6) account for the trajectory of Taiwan’s democratisation and cross-Strait relations; and (7) deliver a research-grade case study and reflection note that engage critically with primary scholarship.

課程簡介:
Today’s world is becoming more interconnected and globalized. Public health issues — such as infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and emerging technologies — are no longer national or regional problems; they are increasingly addressed through a global, integrated, and multidisciplinary approach.
This course empowers students, future policy-makers, and practitioners to analyze and engage with global health issues. Each week introduces a topic in global health governance — such as the World Health Organization and the International Health Regulations, pandemic preparedness, climate change and human health, health technology and digital health, health financing, and One Health — led by the instructors or invited guest speakers. Reflecting recent World Health Assembly priorities, the 2026 edition gives expanded attention to climate change and human health, health technology, and the financing of global health.
In the final weeks, the class executes a simulated public health emergency under the World Health Organization framework (the WHO Simulation), joined by outside experts, civil society, and journalists. Students are divided into four to five countries and assigned roles as key legal, policy, and public health decision-makers responding to the scenario. The simulation consolidates what students learn across the term and builds their competencies in global health governance.
課程目標與學習成效:
•  Understand current global health issues and risks, including emerging infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, climate change, and the role of new health technologies.
•  Understand how global health governance works — its institutions, strengths, and weaknesses in addressing global health challenges.
•  Develop the ability to participate in international conferences, deliver oral presentations, and collaborate in teams.
•  Build research capabilities using media, literature, and databases, and gain front-line experience of health policy-making through the WHO Simulation.
•  Broaden horizons beyond students’ own disciplines, deepening understanding of public health, biomedicine, law, and international relations.

115-1課表備註: 不收低年級學生；土資土測組選修
課程簡介: 本課程旨在建立土地使用管制之基本理念並說明其應用情形。課程內容為除介紹土地使用管制的基本理論與現行土地使用管制制度（包括土地使用分區管制（zoning）與開發許可制(planning permission)等）外，亦對土地市場在土地使用管制下的運作與問題進行論。主要內容分為四部分，1.介紹土地使用管制之基本理念，以及土地使用分區管制之形成、基本精神、制度內容及制度的延伸應用。並以美國土地使用分區管制為例，說明形成土地使用分區管制制度的財產權爭議、規範及執行。2.說明開發許可制之形成、基本精神及制度內容為主軸，並以英國執行開發許可制為例，介紹制度的演進與改變、以及在執行開發許可時，對土地市場之影響。3.說明臺灣實施土地使用分區管制與非都市土地使用管制之背景、現行制度內容與制度執行情形，同時探討土地使用分區管制之實行對於土地市場之影響。4.介紹未來實施國土計畫法中有關土地土地使用管制的理念及可能的執行方式，以及與現行土地使用管制制度的銜接情形。
課程目標與學習成效: 建立土地使用管制之基本理念、介紹土地使用管制之相關制度(如土地使用分區管制與(zoning)及開發許可制(planning permission)，討論台灣地區土地使用管制(都市土地與非都市土地)之內涵。讓同學瞭解土地市場中土地使用管制之角色，並對土地資源配置之利用政策與土地／不動產市場進行分析。

課程簡介:
Cartography is the technique, science, and art of transforming data into maps.
These maps help us see and understand complex spatial patterns and relationships in a visual way.
Maps are everywhere --- they are part of our daily lives, often used without us even noticing. While traditional paper maps are still important, they have largely been replaced or supplemented by digital maps. However, the core idea of turning data into useful visual information remains the same. Thanks to the digital revolution, cartography has undergone major changes and successfully adapted to modern tools and technologies.
This course introduces students to
Digital Cartography
by focusing on how maps are made --- from choosing and organizing data, to filtering and interpreting it, to designing clear, effective maps. Students will explore these steps while creating their own maps using powerful digital tools.
Because of its ability to store, manage, analyze and visualize spatial data,
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
plays a central role in this process. Throughout the course, students will use GIS to support their cartographic work and bring their map ideas to life.
In addition to traditional cartographic concepts, the course introduces students to modern technologies, including
Machine Learning (ML)
, that are beginning to influence how maps are made, interpreted, and automated. Students will gain foundational insights into how ML techniques can be used to classify spatial data, detect patterns, or assist in map generalization and feature extraction, helping them understand the growing role of intelligent systems in the future of cartography.
課程目標與學習成效:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the theoretical and practical foundations of cartography and map design in the digital age. It emphasizes how spatial data is transformed into effective visual communication through maps. Students will gain hands-on experience using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and be introduced to state-of-the-art technologies, such as Machine Learning tools for mapping,  hat are reshaping the way spatial data is analyzed and visualized.
Map creation will focus on a variety of use cases, including physical maps, charts and plans, complex thematic maps incorporating relevant topics such as hazard mapping and Sustainable Development Goals (in particular SDG 11 and 15), and topological maps (network maps)
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Understand and apply core cartographic concepts, including scale, projection, generalization, and symbolization.
Identify, evaluate, and select appropriate spatial data for specific mapping purposes.
Design effective map concepts that reflect the intended message and audience.
Transform raw data into higher-level, interpretable information through filtering, classification, and visual hierarchy.
Produce digital maps using standard cartographic techniques and GIS tools that adhere to principles of effective visual communication.
Use international cartographic terminology to describe and critique their map products.
Gain foundational awareness of how AI and machine learning are used in cartography, e.g., in automating feature recognition, supporting data generalization, or enhancing spatial pattern detection.
Critically assess the strengths and limitations of AI-supported mapping workflows.

課程簡介:
民法是地政領域相當重要的法學基礎科目，雖然是處理人民與人民間的法律關係，但因為民法為萬法之母，因此，無論是不動產交易、土地開發，甚至土地行政都會與民法的基礎觀念有密切的關聯性。民法的內容主要包括財產法及家族法，前者可以說是處理一般市民的法律行為，包括債編及物權編；後者則處理家族之間的身分關係及財產關係，包括親屬編及繼承編。這些篇章的基本運作邏輯及規範則另外規範於總則編，包括權利主體、權利客體及法律行為等概念，都是許多法律關係會運用到的觀念，可以認為是所有民事法律關係運作的基礎。
本學期主要著重在民法總則編及債編總論債之效力前基本概念的介紹，由於涉及基本概念的建構，課程主要由教師講授，透過案例的方式協助同學理解，並輔以討論確保同學對於基本概念的掌握度。由於課程時間有限，不可能逐一講解各個條文，因此，主要針對重要的法律概念及條文規範做討論，並讓同學可以了解到各個法律規範的立法目的、立法理由，並希望同學們可以透過學習，有能力面對具體個別的案件時，找出正確的條文，並有基本的法律解釋能力。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程主要的目的在於透過學習，讓同學有以下的學習成效：
1.具備深度閱讀的能力：希望同學透過課堂的學習及對於課堂資料的研讀，對於民法的基本理念及立法意旨有所了解，並有能力閱讀並正確理解法院判決，提升基礎學養的厚度。
2.具備有效運用大學各項學習資源：本校有諸多圖書及資料庫的資源，希望同學有能力查找資訊，運用工作來解決問題。
3.養成自主與終身學習的態度與策略：讓同學了解到法律規範及法律解釋往往需與時俱進，因此，需要隨時掌握社會脈動，對民法的相關發展有所掌握。

課程簡介: 極端降雨與複合型災害日益頻繁的背景下，水災、坡地崩塌與土砂運移等環境現象已成為國土環境風險的重要來源。本課程以「環境數值模擬」為核心，帶領土地資訊與測量組學生建立從物理機制到空間化成果的完整能力鏈：理解水文與土砂運移等基本過程、掌握模型所需之輸入資料（如 DEM、土地覆蓋、土壤/地質、降雨歷線等）與前處理方法、學習模型參數與邊界條件設定，並透過校驗、敏感度分析與不確定性表達，判讀模擬結果的可信度與適用範圍。課程將以淹水範圍、水深/流速、沖刷與堆積熱區、土石流可能路徑與影響範圍等為主要輸出，進一步轉換為可在 GIS 中整合之災害潛勢圖資與指標，並示範其在都市與國土相關工作中的支援角色，例如：潛在熱區辨識、基礎設施與聚落暴露度盤點、不同情境下風險差異比較，以及跨領域溝通所需的技術性說明。整體目標在於培養學生具備「理解模型—產出圖資—解讀限制」的專業素養，使其能以一致且可檢核的量化方法支撐環境風險之空間分析與應用。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程將介紹都會與山區天災類型與風險評估、數值地形於災害判釋原則與
防災韌性與國土調適策略
。課程將學習以遙測圖資及GIS工具產製災害潛勢圖之基本原則、圖資來源與分析方法等，支援都市與國土防災相關應用之技術溝通：能以技術語言清楚說明潛勢成果、資料需求與限制，並示範與土地利用、建物、基礎設施等資料的疊合與暴露度盤點方法。
課程中亦將教授災害數值模擬核心概念，包含理解環境數值模擬之基本概念、控制方程與主要假設，說明模型適用尺度與限制條件。同時學習掌握輸入資料與前處理流程，具備整備 DEM圖資分析、土地使用、降雨歷線、土壤/地質等關鍵資料之能力，理解資料品質對模擬結果的影響。完成基本建模與情境設定建立可重複之模擬流程，並進行多情境（現況/極端/假設情境）比較。透過判讀結果可信度：能執行校驗與敏感度分析，辨識誤差來源，並以合理方式呈現不確定性與結果解讀界線。最終產製不同災害類型之潛勢圖資與指標：將模擬輸出轉換為 GIS 可用的潛勢圖層與空間指標（如土砂災害範圍、沖刷堆積熱區、影響熱區等），建構國土防災與空間分析基礎情資之能力。

課程簡介:
本課程聚焦不動產估價產業兩項核心且高度專業的業務--都市更新權利變換估價，以及容積移轉與容積代金估價。兩者皆配合都市計畫運作，專業性與複雜性兼具；課程分為兩大部分，分別建立其法令框架、估價技術與實務操作能力。
一、都市更新權利變換估價（第1–9週）
依都市更新條例第五章及都市更新權利變換實施辦法，權利人以更新前之土地、合法建物及他項權利參與更新，於更新後按「更新前權利價值比率」分配更新後之土地、建築物或權利金。課程探討權利變換估價之主要對象——更新前權利價值（土地權利價值與比例、合法建物殘值、租金補償、舊違章戶處理）、更新後總權利價值，以及共同負擔（公共設施用地、工程費用、權利變換費用、貸款利息、稅捐、管理費及容積獎勵／移轉所支付費用等）之計算與折價抵付，並說明評價基準日（權利變換計畫報核前六個月）與權益分配機制。法令與技術依據包括不動產估價技術規則第124至128條、各縣市估價報告書範本及審查注意事項，以及估價師全聯會第六號公報（都市更新權利變換不動產估價報告書範本）。
二、容積移轉與容積代金估價（第10–16週）
本部分沿「從容積移轉（TDR）到容積代金、再到跨基地容積調配」的制度演進主軸，引導同學理解發展權如何成為可定價、可治理的資產。先以國際視野（空中權 Air Rights、TDR 與開發利益回饋、紐約中央車站）切入，續談台灣 TDR 兩階段演進（古蹟與大稻埕歷史街區保存，到公共設施保留地取得）與送出基地五大類型；再進入容積代金之核心估價邏輯——以「容移前／容移後」雙情境比較、土地開發分析法為主、比較法與收益法為輔，並佐以實務案例（如士林科技園區企業總部之容積代金估價）說明定價流程。法令依據包括都市計畫容積移轉實施辦法、各縣市容積移轉自治法規與代金估價報告書範本，估價技術另參酌估價師公會所發布之相關公報以及通用原則。
課程結合估價師全聯會技術公報、各縣市政府估價報告書範本與多個個案實例，並安排權利變換估價說明會與容積代金說明簡報之模擬演練；修課同學最後以分組個案報告展現學習成果。
課程目標與學習成效:
課程目標：
將估價理論與方法運用於不同的土地開發或都市計畫執行業務上，讓同學了解權利變換估價及容積代金估價的核心關注與實務運用的細節。
學習成效：
具備都市更新權利變換之基本概念與法令框架。
具備運用估價技術於權利變換權益分配（更新前後價值、共同負擔）之能力。
具備容積移轉制度與發展權貨幣化（容積代金）之基本概念。
具備以雙情境比較及土地開發分析法評估容積代金之技術。
具備向報告書使用人（主管機關、實施者與權利人）清楚說明估價結論之溝通能力。

TL;DR
. Learn how to make smarter, evidence‑based decisions about real‑world spatial problems.
We start with core decision‑making tools, then dive into GIS, spatial analysis, and machine learning to tackle challenges like planning infrastructure, mapping hazards, and shaping land‑use policy. By the end, we will be able to design, run, and evaluate powerful spatial decision workflows from the ground up.
Long Version.
How can we make better decisions about places, spaces, and the world around us?
This course explores the tools and approaches that help answer that question.
It begins with the basics of decision-making — breaking down complex choices into manageable steps and comparing options in a structured way. Core methods such as
multi‑criteria analysis, weighting techniques,
and
simple statistical models
provide a foundation for understanding robust decision processes.
During the  second half of the semester, the focus then shifts to
spatial problems
— those that involve geography and location. Using
Geographic Information Systems (GIS),
the class works through real-world challenges including site selection, infrastructure planning, hazard zone mapping, and land-use policy evaluation. Hands-on labs demonstrate how
Spatial Decision Support Systems (SDSS)
are designed, adapted, and assessed for different decision contexts.
The course introduces
machine learning
approaches — including
decision trees, logistic regression,
and
clustering
— to identify patterns in decision-making. Spatial machine learning models and feature ranking strategies add a leading‑edge complement to traditional analysis.
By the end of the semester, we will have the skills to:
Apply GIS and integrated tools to address spatial decision problems,
Design and implement complete decision‑making workflows,
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of decision processes.
Relevant to fields such as
urban planning, environmental analysis, disaster management,
and
policy design,
the course equips students with a practical toolkit for evidence‑based spatial decision making.
課程目標與學習成效:
Course Goals
This course aims to:
Explore key theories, methods, and tools for spatial decision making.
Examine case studies from the literature to highlight successful applications and common challenges.
Provide hands‑on experience in the design, implementation, and evaluation of spatial decision workflows.
Integrate Geographic Information Systems (GIS), statistical methods, and machine learning techniques to support evidence‑based decisions.
Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course, we will be able to:
Identify and critically assess existing spatial decision-making projects from academic and applied contexts.
Select and adapt appropriate approaches for a given decision problem.
Collect, prepare, and model spatial and non‑spatial data for analysis.
Design and implement a complete spatial decision workflow, from problem definition to outcome evaluation.
Apply GIS software and integrated modelling tools to create a targeted decision-making system from scratch.
Incorporate statistical and machine learning methods to analyse patterns and improve decision outcomes.
Evaluate the robustness and reliability of conclusions based on multiple criteria, variables, and uncertainty considerations.

課程簡介: 在社會科學的領域中，如果說有什麼學問應該以台灣作為研究典範的，無疑是國際貿易了。台灣自與西方文明世界接觸的四百年來，都是以貿易為立足點，因此台灣經濟充分展現國際分工的特色，發揮專業生產的利益。無論是狩獵時代、農業時代、工業時代或者是「新經濟」時代，台灣均曾利用對外貿易達成資源的有效運用和經濟的成長。因為外在環境和內部政治局勢的演變，台灣在貿易政策上曾經歷鎖國、開港、貿易保護、貿易擴張等不同的時代。

課程簡介:
This course is designed to introduce to undergraduate and postgraduate students the pertinent economic theories and their applications to contemporary environmental problems. We will firstly introduce the Economics-based analytical approaches for environmental studies. We particularly focus on contemporary environmental issues such as pollution, greenhouse gases emissions and virtual trade of natural resources. Secondly we will discuss the literature on the nexus between trade, national economy and sustainability. Countries derive additional economic benefits from trade than otherwise, for example, with augmented domestic production. Natural environment and resources are used as input for producing exported goods (or to accommodate pollutants discharged from the production process). However, environmental stress concomitant with the economic boom was not properly attended nor charged. Typical of such case, Asian-Pacific economies are attracting the world’s attention in their rapid economic growth, sizable markets and increasingly significant role in the global economy. Domestic and global factors have together shaped the diverse economies in this region, particularly in their economic structure and development pathways and strategies. Inextricably linked with economic activities, environmental quality and natural resource endowment in this region are facing tremendous stress from far and near. Developed and developing countries of this region share a common development experience by thriving their economies on trade, though now even more intensive globalization. Sustainable development in both the economy and environment is thus concerned. A good grasp of the economy-environment nexus from both economy-wide and world-wide perspectives is imperative and helpful in guiding pertinent policies to effectively tackle the dual challenge of sustainability transition.
The course participants are encouraged to get involved in the discussion on issues and analyses particularly from the perspectives of economics, and to summarize in the form of academic writing the insights and policy implications derived from the literature review. Students will form small groups to present and discuss on selected papers. Presentations of the group projects by the students on their literature review of pertinent theories, applications and policy assessment will culminate with the course.
The topics we will review of literature centering the nexus of trade, economy and the environment, mainly from economic perspectives, are:
The nexus between trade, economy and the environment,
Environment impact of economic activities,
Natural resource leakage from developing countries,
Economic development pathways and strategies of the developed countries, and their experiences in managing the concomitant environmental stress,
Economic analysis on policies for correcting negative externality of economic activities, and
Measures proposed for green growth.
The participants will get experience in doing academic literature review and writing-up, in addition to the knowledge of trade and environmental economic theories.

課程簡介:
經濟學是一門強調精確的社會科學，精確不意味能無誤地進行分析預測，而是明確地呈現分析的方式，讓自己與其他人能客觀判斷分析過程的合理性與有效性。數學提供了一個共同的語言讓經濟學研究者得以精準地彼此溝通，同時它的分析架構也協助研究者能依照一定的程序去解決問題。
本門課將著重介紹線性代數(linear algebra)，因為它是一個分析複雜經濟關係的重要數學工具。一般均衡理論、投入產出模型與計量經濟學等領域，都仰賴向量與矩陣來表示多變數方程組。線性代數讓經濟學家能同時分析多個相互影響的變數，有助於理解市場均衡、穩定性與政策效果。此外，機器學習在經濟研究中的應用日益普及，而線性迴歸、神經網路與主成分分析等方法，都建立在線性代數基礎之上。因此，扎實的線性代數能力能提升經濟理論的理解與資料分析的能力。
課程目標與學習成效:
1. 熟悉線性代數的內涵與分析方法.
2. 學習將線性代數應用於經濟議題分析.
3. 為學生在大數據及進階經濟課程打好數學基礎.

課程簡介:
International trade is the economic backbone of most countries in the world. The development of information technologies has pushed forward the trade facilitation and digitalization of cross border exchange. The digital transformation of international trade has reduced the operation time and costs, facilitated the global value chain, and connected the trade and logistics communities globally.
Cross border digital trade attracts higher attention than ever in the post COVID-19 era. While normal international trade procedures and operations which are heavily dependent on paper-documents are interrupted, the use of technologies helps to make the international trade more resilient and lower the barriers of physical documentation. International initiatives as well as respective government’s actions in the implementation of cross border digital trade to increase the scale, scope and speed of trade will be introduced in this course. Challenges including the adoption of new technologies, policy and regulation issues, change of user behavior during the implementation of cross border digital trade will also be discussed in the course.
This course aims to develop students’ knowledge about the digitalization of international trade for increasing their competitive edges in the global business setting.

Course Objectives:
This course is targeted at achieving the following objectives:
To enable students with knowledge of cross border digital trade
To equip students with the knowledge of the emerging information technologies in international trade
To prepare students who wish to enter into global trade businesses

Course Description
What is economic anthropology, and how is it different from the discipline of economics? One answer, the answer that this class is based on, is this: “
economic
transactions are always already
social
relations” (Ho 2021). This means they are also
political
relations,
moral
relations,
ecological
relations, and also
cosmological
relations. A century of ethnographic research and anthropological theory has long challenged the assumptions of mainstream economics that people start as self-maximizing individuals and only enter into relationships to “trade and barter.” On the other hand, to say that economic transactions are always already relational and social, or that many peoples engage in “moral economies” does not mean these are necessarily equitable or devoid of self-interest. Furthermore, the world has long been interconnected, especially over the last few centuries, within global capitalism. Capitalism is also a form of relationality, but how is it different or similar to non-capitalist relations? In this class, we will examine the relationality of economic life at multiple scales, across times, and across geographical locations and cultural contexts. We will address key concepts such as exchange, production, labor, commodification, gender, land, racialization, infrastructure, colonialism, development, debt, inequality, value, and the work of nature. Through readings, discussion, films, guest speakers, fieldtrips, and participatory ethnographic work, students will learn to see the “economy” in terms of its social, political, ecological, and ethical stakes, and consider how economic anthropology sheds insights on the problem of living and surviving together on the same planet.
Goals and Learning Outcomes:
-Understand the distinct approaches to the “economic” offered by anthropology.
-Understand the social, political, and ethical implications of economic relations.
-Understand the meaning, significance and application of concepts like “the gift,” “capitalism”, “value,” “distribution” and “debt”
-Understand the relation between the state and ethnic groups in terms of capitalism and development
-Understand the cultural bases for movements seeking economic justice and livelihoods.

What's a discussion question?
You are expected to read the assigned readings and be ready to discuss them in class. To facilitate
discussion, I ask everyone to post a short response to the reading on the class website discussion board by 5PM the night before class. These responses should pose questions which directly engage the major
arguments and/or examples provided by the author(s). They may address something you find particularly interesting, surprising, confusing, or frustrating about the reading. In each case, be sure to elaborate your points with reference to the text. The question should not just repeat the readings, demand a simple yes/no answer, or demand knowledge beyond the readings. Rather, it pursues clarification or exploration by posing a question that takes you deeper into the text. Not every discussion question has a clear answer—most don’t—nor do most take a debate format (i.e., posing contrasting positions and asking people to argue them). Most discussion questions can be posed in a sentence but might require an additional sentence or two of explication, contextualization or follow-up. Also, it is helpful to refer to specific keywords or page numbers to guide fellow readers to key passages in the texts or ideas raised in lecture.
Discussion Leading
Starting later in the semester, several students will be asked each session to lead the beginning of class discussion. This means preparing beforehand to introduce the reading, and to pose some discussion questions for the class. Please prepare several slides (PPT or similar software) as a visual aid for your classmates. I will make a sign-up sheet available beforehand, but if there are topics you are particularly interested in, you may let me know earlier.
Final Paper
You will apply the themes, questions, approaches, and/or research methods from the course to understand a case study of your own choosing. The case study should be something of personal interest to you, but it should broadly concern the themes of the course: particularly the social, cultural, and/or political meanings of a concrete "economic" phenonomon or situation. The case study should involve original research outside the class materials. There is flexibility regarding the kind of materials you can use. You might chose a case that involves reading relevant articles and/or books. Or you might conduct your own research through interviews or participant observation. Or you might analyze particular forms of media. You may also draw on the fieldwork assignments for inspiration, provided that you expand on them. When writing the paper, you should draw on the course themes, readings, and discussions to interpret or compare the data.
You should begin thinking about topics of interest from the start of the course, but must submit a half-page proposal to me by Week 12 (11/26) so I can review and approve the topic, and offer any relevant suggestions. I also request that you arrange a 15-min office hour meeting with me starting this week or after to discuss your proposal in more detail. If Thursday afternoon is not convenient, please let me know ahead of time.
On Week 15 or 16 (12/17 or 12/24), you will be asked to deliver a short presentation on your topic in class. This is not a formal presentation, but be prepared to discuss the project. The goal is to share ideas and get feedback, and not to be graded on presentation.
The paper itself should be 10 Pages, Double-Spaced, Times New Roman; or about 2,500 Words (English), or 4,000 Words (Chinese).
Academic Integrity
You are expected to be honest in all of your academic work. Allegations of alleged academic dishonesty will be forwarded to the administration. Sanctions for academic dishonesty can include failing grades and/or suspension from the university. Mid-terms and the Final Paper must be properly cited. Please see
https://www.chicagomanualofstyle.org/home.html
for information on how to properly cite. Please note that LLMs often hallucinate citations, so double-check if you use an LLM to recall a page number.
Large Language Models, otherwise known as “AI,” are useful for polishing writing, but they have also made it easy to automatically generate essays and discussion questions. However, I trust you are taking this class because you find the topic interesting and have no intention of wasting the opportunity. The written assignments are an opportunity to engage with the readings, lectures, and discussions. If you take the time and engage, I will respond to you as a person assuming that I am speaking with a real person.

課程簡介:
本課程為民族學系大一必修，本課程介紹臺灣多元族群文化之形成與議題。教學方式包含教師講課、分組討論、專題報告、紀錄片賞析，預計透過多元教學方式使同學以民族學的視野認識臺灣社會的族群議題，進而思考民族學於當代社會之應用。
本課程採用台灣的五大族群分類說──原住民族、客家人、閩南人、外省人和新移民──來做為每周課程授課的綱要，但為使大一學生也能培養以民族學視野來認識台灣社會的能力，在每週課程中也會同時以六大議題來解析民族誌，六大民族學議題包含：民族社會、民族經濟、民族政治、民族宗教、民族歷史、民族生態。
本課程上課方式為前兩節教師講課，第三堂課為同學導讀與討論。將於開學第一週將學生分組，並依每週進度排定一組導讀、一組提問，導讀組針對指定文獻進行25分鐘的導讀（會計時，時間到即結束導讀），提問組針對指定文獻提出三～四個問題讓學生上課時討論。透過導讀／提問的設計，希望能培養學生深度閱讀臺灣民族誌之批判性思考能力，以及思考如何應用民族學於臺灣當代族群議題。另有安排客座演講與移地教學。

課程簡介: 本課程大綱為一學年教學設計。旨在培養學生對於當代泰雅族語言文化發展能有基本認識，奠定語言學習之基礎。透過對台灣原住民族泰雅族語之學習，瞭解其民族社會文化之內涵，進而培養觀察記錄及比較研究之能力。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程教學之「泰雅語」，係針對「
Kinhakul
」，即昔日民族學、語言學所分類之「
Squliq
賽考列克群」方言，
2002
年行政院原民會族語認證分類所謂之「賽考利克泰雅語」。
上課主要教材為教育部與行政院原民會共同發行之「國民中小學九年一貫課程原住民族語賽考利克泰雅語學習手冊第一階」；輔助教材為《泰雅族語文化教材》。上述兩教材，前者作為初接觸泰雅語學習者之入門基礎教材，後者則為促進學習者對泰雅族語言及社會文化之認識。上課內容除此兩教材並延伸介紹討論之議題外，儘可能地做方言間之對照比較，並與教師個人之田野經驗暨相關採集素材，歷來泰雅族研究之相關文獻進行對話討論。
本課程除引介比較泰雅語書面文字化發展歷程中之各家語音書寫符號使用及相關之紀錄、現行各式泰雅族語教材等基礎語言教學外，並配合與泰雅族相關之歷史、地理、社會、文化等面向之題材，俾使修課同學透過語言的學習，對於「泰雅民族語言文化」、「台灣原住民族社會與文化變遷」等議題能有更為深入與寬廣的學習視野。
為加強語言學習，課後宜連結泰雅語線上教學之相關網站點選「數位學習」，即可進行反覆練習，累績單字及熟悉句型。
本課程的教學亦會對泰雅族社會文化議題的後續發展進行關注。當代新興的部落生態旅遊及文化展演、人文導覽除了受國內外旅遊業所關注，亦是部落生存發展的熱門話題。如何從學習泰雅語的過程來了解泰雅族的社會人文、山川地景、自然資源以及文化資產也是本課程連帶希望達到的目標之一。理解當代泰雅語的基本知識，培養具備初步的書寫聽讀能力。同在文化、生態多樣性的認知下，尊重多元民族文化及其延續發展的機制，以及強化對於台灣原住民族相關問題的思考與解讀力度。

課程簡介:
本課程介紹語言學的基本概念、理論發展與分析方法，旨在引導大一學生理解人類語言如何被系統性地觀察、描述與研究。課程內容涵蓋句法、音韻、語意、構詞與語用等語言形式分析傳統，同時介紹語言人類學對語言與文化研究的學術貢獻。透過語言學與語言人類學的並置，本課程將協助學生理解語言結構、語言使用、文化意義、社會關係與權力差異之間的關聯，並認識當代語言研究的跨領域取向。
課程為大一必修課，以教師講授為主，並配合指定閱讀、作業、課堂討論與小組報告等方式進行。課程採用中英文教材並行，透過中文教材與課堂講解協助學生掌握基礎概念，同時引導學生逐步接觸英文語言學術語與經典理論，理解閱讀英文學術文獻的重要性。課程前半部以語言學基本概念與形式分析為主；期中考之後，則轉向語言與社會文化、語言意識形態、多語現象、跨語實踐、數位媒介與跨領域研究等主題，說明語言學知識在不同研究領域中的運用。
因應生成式 AI 與大型語言模型的發展，本課程也將納入「AI 與語言學的批判分析」。課程不將 AI 視為標準答案，而是將其作為批判性探究與反思的起點，引導學生運用語言學與語言人類學概念，檢視 AI 生成內容在文法、翻譯、語音、口音、方言、語言變異與語言文化議題上的回答。學生將分析其中可能出現的概念混淆、過度簡化、語言偏見、文化盲點與知識限制，並練習以書寫方式清楚表達對語言、文化、AI 科技與知識生產關係的批判觀點。
課程目標與學習成效:
（一）引導大一學生認識語言學的基本概念、理論發展與分析方法，理解人類語言如何被系統性地觀察、描述與研究，並建立修習後續語言學、民族語言、人類學與語言人類學相關課程所需的基礎知識。
（二）協助學生掌握句法、音韻、語意、構詞與語用等語言形式分析的基本內容，培養學生觀察、描述與初步分析語言結構及語言現象的能力。
（三）透過語言學與語言人類學的並置，引導學生理解語言不僅是形式系統，也是一種社會文化實踐，並能思考語言結構、語言使用、文化意義、社會關係、身分認同與權力差異之間的關聯。
（四）透過中英文教材並行、課堂講授、指定閱讀、作業、討論與小組報告，協助學生熟悉語言學基本術語與英文學術概念，逐步建立閱讀英文學術文獻與表達學術觀點的能力。
（五）引導學生將課程所學運用於分析臺灣及其他社會中的多語現象、跨語實踐、語言意識形態、數位媒介與語言文化議題，培養學生尊重多語、多文化與不同語言實踐差異的態度。
（六）結合當代生成式 AI 與大型語言模型的發展，訓練學生運用語言學與語言人類學概念，批判性檢視 AI 生成內容中可能出現的概念混淆、過度簡化、語言偏見、文化盲點與知識限制。
（七）培養學生以書面作業與課堂討論清楚表達對語言、文化、AI 科技與知識生產之間關係的分析與批判觀點，使學生能在生成式 AI 日益影響語言使用、翻譯實踐與學習方式的時代，具備基礎而反思性的語言分析能力。

115
學年度第一學期的教學目標將社會情緒學習導入課程，透過閱讀分析民族誌工作者在進行民族誌調查方法時的情緒變化，理解情緒如何影響調查，以及如何感知並克服情緒之影響，完成研究調查任務，並撰寫出引人入勝的民族誌作品。
課程目標與學習成效:
本學年課程將分成五大階段，上學期目標包含前三階段，下學期目標完成後兩階段：
第一，閱讀與討論民族誌作品並分析其方法；
第二，學習並操練民族學田野調查方法；
第三，完成研究計畫書初稿，
第四，利用寒假探索田野場域並建立關係；
第五，下學期進入專題調查實作並完成學年報告。
關於社會情緒學習在上述各階段的具體操作與嵌入方式，以下分述之：
學生透過閱讀民族誌作品理解何為民族誌方法，以及理解民族誌工作者因自己的 身份、位置、年齡與性別等等差異，針對不同議題在不同情境、年代與場域運用 民族誌方法所面臨的困難與克服困難的策略。
教師引導學生聚焦在民族誌工作者在進行田野調查過程中所經歷的情緒狀況，並分析這些情況如何影響研究者的調查工作與成果。每篇閱讀都會有相關的課程活動，並請學生撰寫課程參與筆記，並練習

藉由在
校園與家庭場域
進行民族誌方法的操練，作為進入實作場域前的暖身工作。
教師藉由三次田野方法之操作，要求學生進行田野筆記，每次筆記中有一欄是紀錄自己的情緒情況，並反思這些情緒如何影響方法的操作。
選擇一個議題(需包含相關場域與人群)，進行民族誌寫作之專題提案。

課程簡介: This graduate course examines nomadic traditions of Central Asian peoples as living, evolving practices rather than relics of the past. Drawing on ethnography, oral history, material culture studies, and contemporary fieldwork, students will explore how nomadic ways of life—pastoral herding, portable architecture, oral epic poetry, seasonal migrations, and traditional crafts—continue to shape daily life, identity, and community across the region today. Special attention is given to how nomadic heritage is negotiated, preserved, and transformed in the context of modernization, urbanization, and state-building in the post-Soviet era. The course combines thematic lectures with guest seminars by scholars and practitioners from Central Asia.
課程目標與學習成效:
Course Objectives:
To introduce students to nomadic traditions as dynamic, living cultural systems in Central Asia
To examine the material, social, and symbolic dimensions of nomadic life—from yurts and herding to oral poetry and ritual
To analyze how nomadic traditions are preserved, adapted, or contested in modern Central Asian societies
To develop students' ability to use ethnographic and comparative methods in analyzing non-Western cultural practices
To foster cross-cultural understanding through direct engagement with scholars and practitioners from the region
Learning Outcomes:
Students will be able to identify and describe key nomadic traditions across different Central Asian groups
Students will critically analyze the relationship between nomadic heritage and contemporary identity politics
Students will demonstrate understanding of how material culture, oral traditions, and everyday practices intersect
Students will develop comparative analytical skills applicable to cultural studies and area studies research
Students will engage productively with primary sources—including oral testimonies, ethnographic texts, and cultural artifacts

課程簡介:
This is a theoretically oriented seminar course focusing on the historiography, theories, and contemporary developments of linguistic anthropology, including the emerging linguistic anthropology of AI. The purpose of this course is to explore how linguistic anthropologists conduct research to foreground language practices within a matrix of cultural dynamics, power relations, social inequality, and identity construction. Different from formal analyses of language, linguistic anthropologists view language as social action through which meaning, language ideology, subjectivity, identity, voice, and power are constituted, contested, and transformed across time and space.
The course also examines how artificial intelligence, especially large language models and other AI-based language technologies, challenges and extends core questions in linguistic anthropology. AI-generated language raises important issues about interaction, communicative competence, authorship, voice, authority, knowledge production, and human–machine communication. By bringing classical theories of linguistic anthropology into dialogue with contemporary debates on AI, this course asks how language continues to mediate social life in an increasingly machine-mediated communicative world.
本課程為
EMI
課程(使用英語、華語)，以語言人類學的學術知識史、理論發展與當代理論思潮為核心，開放給大學部高年級與碩士班學生選修。本課程旨在引導學生理解語言人類學如何研究語言實踐，並將語言置於文化動態、權力關係、社會不平等、身分建構、主體性與聲音等問題的交織脈絡中加以分析。不同於以語言形式結構為主要對象的語言學分析，語言人類學將語言視為一種社會行動，關注語言如何在具體互動情境、社會文化脈絡與歷史過程中，參與意義、語言意識形態、身分認同、主體性、聲音與權力關係的形成、協商與爭辯。本課程將系統性討論人類學與語言學在「語言與文化」研究中的主要論述與基礎理論，並透過民族誌案例與實際語言資料，訓練學生連結理論概念與經驗分析。

To cultivate students’ understanding of the historiography, classical theories, and contemporary developments of linguistic anthropology through the systematic reading of foundational texts, and to help them grasp how linguistic anthropologists analyze language practices within broader contexts of cultural dynamics, power relations, social inequality, and identity formation.
B. To train students to use core concepts in linguistic anthropology to analyze language as social action, through which meaning, language ideology, subjectivity, identity, voice, and authority are constituted, negotiated, contested, and transformed across time and space.
C. To develop students’ ability to connect micro-level linguistic practices with broader political-economic, sociocultural, and historical processes, and to cultivate more nuanced and critical forms of observation and analysis.

To guide students in examining how artificial intelligence, especially large language models and AI-based language technologies, challenges and extends central questions in linguistic anthropology, including interaction, communicative competence, authorship, voice, authority, knowledge production, and human–machine communication.

課程簡介:
博物館學Museology是以蒐藏品為核心，博物館以蒐藏品為核心，圍繞著蒐藏品作為一種「物」出發，進一步透過展覽、說明與舉辦活動，以博物館為載體與媒介，將蒐藏品連結到人、社區與社會，也就是建立起博物館與文化資產的關聯性。在這個連結的過程中，如何將蒐藏品這個「物」原本所處的文化脈絡，藉由博物館的展示與說明，重新被賦予一個當代社會的脈絡，與觀眾、社區與社會連結在一起。其中，最為核心的問題就是，這些蒐藏品作為「物」，原本所處的文化脈絡是什麼？其「社會生命史」又是什麼？本課程由四個部分展開：
第一單元、博物館的歷史與發展
第二單元、博物館與物質文化研究(Material Culture Studies)
第三單元、批判的文化遺產研究：博物館化(museumification)/遺產化(heritagization)的現象與議題
第四單元、博物館人類學（Museum Anthropology）視野下的族群文化
課程目標與學習成效: 博物館作為一個當代公共知識生產的機構，如何組織、描述並說明這些藏品複雜且豐富的背景，其實也就是一個描述與說明何謂文化資產的過程。關於不同社會中「物」與人的關係，一直是人類學研究中物質文化領域最為重視的關懷。對人類學的物質文化研究有所掌握，將能夠從不同於當代社會的文化視野來重新思考、描述、說明博物館蒐藏品作為「物」應該如何被說明、不同的文化資產將可以如何展示以及連結到當代社會。

By achieving these learning goals, students should be well-equipped to conduct rigorous and valid statistical analyses in their social science research, contributing to the advancement of knowledge in social sciences.
