課程簡介:
本學期「心理計量專題」以縱貫資料分析（
longitudinal data analysis
）為核心主題，內容涵蓋從古典重複測量方法到當代多層次成長模型、結構方程潛在成長曲線模型、以及交叉延宕追蹤模型之完整方法光譜。課程以一條貫穿全學期的概念主軸開展：組間差異（
between-person differences
）與組內變化（
within-person change
）之區辨，並以此檢視每一種方法對變化歷程的假定與限制。課程強調以
R
語言完整實作分析流程，並使用模擬資料與經典追蹤研究資料作為範例，訓練學生具備從資料整理、遺失值處理、視覺化、模型設定、估計、診斷到結果報告撰寫之完整能力。本課程適合已具備迴歸分析或變異數分析基礎、欲系統性建立縱貫研究方法論能力之心理學系碩士班與博士班研究生修習。
This semester's Special Topics in Psychometrics seminar is organized around longitudinal data analysis, spanning the full methodological range from classical repeated-measures approaches to contemporary multilevel growth models, latent growth curve models within the structural equation modeling framework, and cross-lagged panel model. The course is structured around a single conceptual thread that runs through the entire semester: the distinction between between-person differences and within-person change, which is used to examine what each method assumes about the change process and where its limitations lie. Emphasis is placed on complete analytic implementation in R, using both simulated data and classic longitudinal datasets as running examples, so that students develop end-to-end competence spanning data management, missing-data handling, visualization, model specification, estimation, diagnostics, and results reporting. The course is intended for master's and doctoral students in psychology who have completed a graduate-level course in regression or ANOVA and wish to build systematic competence in longitudinal research methodology.
課程目標與學習成效:
理解縱貫研究設計的邏輯與限制，並能區辨組間差異與組內變化在不同研究問題下的意涵。
具備縱貫資料整理、時間變項建構與資料品質檢核之實作能力。
理解縱貫研究中遺失資料的機制（MCAR/MAR/MNAR），並能執行FIML與多重插補等處理方法。
能以視覺化方法呈現個體與群體層次的變化軌跡，並符合APA圖表規範。
能執行並詮釋古典重複測量分析（配對t檢定、RM-ANOVA/MANOVA、GEE），並說明其相對於多層次模型之限制。
能建立、估計並詮釋多層次成長模型，掌握時間編碼、共變量設定與隨機效果結構之選擇邏輯。
能建立潛在成長曲線模型，並理解其與多層次成長模型之對應關係與各自適用時機。
能辨識交叉延宕追蹤設計（CLPM、RI-CLPM）之因果推論議題與假設限制。
能執行成長混合模型與潛在類別成長分析，辨識縱貫資料中異質性之變化軌跡類型，並掌握類別數決定之判準與潛在風險。
運用R語言（tidyverse、lme4/nlme、lavaan、geepack、survival等套件）完成一項完整之縱貫資料分析專題，並以符合學術寫作規範之方式報告結果。

課程簡介:
【本課程並非特定程式語言的入門課程，不適合無程式設計基礎者選修。】
本課程以 Essentials of Programming Languages（3rd ed., Friedman & Wand）為核心教材，圍繞一個核心洞見展開：「一個程式語言的直譯器，本身也只是一支程式。」理解這件事，會從根本上改變你思考程式設計的方式——你將從語言的「使用者」，蛻變為語言的「設計者」。課程採用直譯器作為表達程式語言語意（semantics）的主要工具。從歸納資料結構出發，建立資料抽象的設計原則，再依序實作一系列逐步演進的直譯器：從 LET、PROC、LETREC（處理 binding、scope、closure）到引入 State（計算效果、store model），最後以型別系統（type system）作結。每一章的語言均在前一章的基礎上疊加，形成貫穿全課程的一條主線。課程以 Racket 作為實作語言。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程旨在讓學生從程式語言的「使用者」蛻變為「設計者」——不再只是學習如何用某一語言寫程式，而是深入理解語言本身的設計原理與語意基礎。
(1) Understand how programming languages work from the inside out, through building interpreters.
(2) Grasp the semantic foundations underlying mainstream language features: scope, closures, higher-order functions, mutable state, and type systems.
(3) Develop the ability to reason precisely about program behavior, independent of any particular language.
(4) Cultivate the mindset of a language designer: knowing not just how language features work, but why they are designed the way they are.

課程簡介: Data-driven computing increasingly depends on high-performance, energy-efficient, reliable, durable, and scalable memory and storage systems. To achieve the diversified design objectives, a number of key technologies have been proposed for memory and storage systems in different application scenarios. In this course, we provide a comprehensive overview of the architecture and key technologies of modern memory/storage systems for graduate students. Specifically, we will discuss the following memory/storage media: (i) magnetic storage media (e.g., CMR, SMR, IMR, MAMR, and HAMR), (ii) NAND flash memory, (iii) persistent memories (PMs), such as phase-change memory (PCM), spin-torque transfer RAM (STT-RAM), resistive RAM (ReRAM), domain wall racetrack memory (DW-RM), and skyrmion racetrack memory (SK RM). From the system view, the caching/buffering designs, data placement and space allocation policies, advanced data structures, data encoding and encryption algorithms, data deduplication algorithms, and hardware software codesign issues will be covered. After taking this course, students will be familiar with the foundational design/working principles, key technologies, and future research/development directions of modern memory/storage systems.
課程目標與學習成效:
Understand the architecture and role of storage systems in computing systems.
Learn about major storage technologies (e.g., HDDs, SSDs, persistent memories).
Explore key concepts such as RAID, file systems, and I/O stacks.
Gain insights into distributed storage, security, and emerging trends.

課程簡介: 本課程為強化學習（Reinforcement Learning, RL）之入門課程，教材採用開放式線上課程《Hands-On Modern RL》，以「實作優先」的路徑進行：先從可執行的程式與實際訓練現象出發（如 CartPole 倒立擺），讓學生觀察智慧體（agent）如何在環境中試誤、並從獎勵回饋中改進行為，再回頭建立背後的理論基礎——包括馬可夫決策過程（MDP）、價值函數與貝爾曼方程、時序差分學習與 Q-learning、深度 Q 網路（DQN）、策略梯度、Actor-Critic 與 PPO。課程後段銜接當前 AI 發展前沿，介紹強化學習在大型語言模型後訓練中的應用，包括 RLHF、偏好對齊（DPO）以及 GRPO／可驗證獎勵（RLVR）之基本原理。

了解強化學習於大型語言模型後訓練之應用（RLHF、DPO、GRPO／RLVR）的基本原理與設計動機。（評量工具：期末考試與課堂討論；評量指標：測驗藍圖）

課程簡介:
This course equips students with foundational and advanced knowledge of web mining, intelligent web systems, and AI-driven web development. It integrates traditional web technologies with contemporary advances in artificial intelligence, including deep learning and large language models (LLMs), to support the design and deployment of intelligent web applications.
Core topics include web data acquisition (e.g., scraping and APIs), taxonomy and knowledge representation, social network analysis, and modern web architectures. The course further explores how AI techniques, such as deep learning, natural language processing, and generative AI, can be embedded into web applications to enable automation, personalization, and adaptive user experiences.
Students will engage in hands-on, project-based learning through both individual and group activities. Python-based implementations and AI-enabled development tools (e.g., model APIs, no/low-code platforms, and prompt-based systems) will be introduced to bridge theory and practice. Emphasis is placed on building end-to-end intelligent systems, including data pipelines, model integration, and deployment.
Additional materials will cover essential web technologies (e.g., RESTful APIs, JSON/XML, CSS), evolving paradigms (e.g., microservices, serverless architecture, progressive web apps), and emerging trends such as AI-assisted development, autonomous agents, and human–AI collaboration in software design.
Students are expected to actively participate in all course activities. Opportunities for self-directed exploration are provided, particularly in areas such as AI ethics, data privacy, security, and scalable system integration. By the end of the course, students will be capable of designing and implementing intelligent, AI-enhanced web systems aligned with current industry practices.

Students are able to acquire knowledge of web mining, intelligent web systems, and AI-driven web development.
Students are able to gain knowledge of deep learning, large language models (LLMs), and generative AI technologies for developing intelligent web applications.
Students are able to apply modern web development techniques to design and implement AI-enhanced web applications.

課程簡介:
為了躲避這學期星期五的三天放假，課程時間異動到星期一；不過星期一還是有兩天假期。
依照學校指示：雖然實體課程只有十六星期，但是依照本校正式公文通知與學則規定，每一學分仍然應該有十八小時的教學規畫。因此在課程網頁的每週規畫表格之前，列有相當規模的自習活動。這些自習活動並非可有可無，而與這一門課開學之後的教學息息相關，也都屬於期中評量與期末評量的範圍。提醒選課同學必須自行複習所列之主題。
這一課程以介紹機器學習與深度學習的基本觀念和相關應用為目的。機器學習是人工智慧領域的重要區塊，近年以來因為計算技術的急速進步，許多過去的理論已經變成實用的技術。這一課程透過介紹許多基本的概念，期望讓選課同學了解機器學習技術的基礎觀念，並且進一步學習如何應用公開軟體來處理實際問題。這一課程將介紹機器學習的數個基本型態，包含監督式學習、非監督式學習、迴歸分析、及以類神經網路為基礎的深度學習；並且延伸到大型模型的討論。
課程中以講解基礎學理為主，同時伴隨程式實例的簡介。在幾乎每一個星期都有的 Moodle 作業中經常會使用到以Python為主的程式實例，期待大家都能兼顧學理與實例。
雖然我們會帶到一些關鍵的Python指令或者套件，但是這不是一門學習 Python 的課程。Python是選修這一門課程的先備能力。體驗機器學習的核心功能，而不建構整個應用系統的話，並不需要學會所有的Python指令。當然如果能隨心所欲應用Python是最好的。

的材料。

mathematical foundations

課程簡介:
半體體的應用非常廣泛，如電腦、手機、車用電子需要的晶片是由半導體所組成，太陽能電池、
LED
、雷射等光電元件大部分也是由半導體材料製作。臺灣的半導體產業鏈所扮演的角色，更是在全世界半導體工業舉足輕重。了解半導體的基礎物理特性，是參與研發半導體相關電子與光電元件的基石。本課程簡介半導體的基礎物理知識，進一步簡介由半導體所構成的重要元件的物理特性，如二極體、電晶體、
CMOS
、太陽能電池、
LED
等。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程首先將學習了解半導體所需要的知識，如導電帶、價電帶、能隙、費米能階與電子能量分佈等概念，並了解半導體加電壓下的電流、電容及光電轉換特性等。接下來將探討不同半導體之間接合、半導體與金屬、氧化物等其他材料接合的電子與光電元件，並了解其運作原理。課程目標為培養學習者，了解並能闡述半導體物理基礎概念的能力，並清楚如何應用在解釋幾個重要的半導體元件特性，具備相關知識可進一步修習進階的半導體元件課程、從事半導體相關研究及接觸半導體產業等。

Also, graph pattern mining is one of the most important topics for graph data mining as well as the pairwise shortest path query and triangle counting. Furthermore, to avoid malice adversary obtaining users’ real identities of each corresponding node, privacy-preserving graph mining plays a very important role when social network data is used in practical commercial sales. The clustering and classification of documents in social media are also important for social networks.

課程簡介:
本課程主要講授JavaScript程式語言與其應用，並引導學生了解AI如何對軟體教育、軟體工程與軟體產業發生影響、培養當代軟體開發人員應具備的AI素養。JavaScript最初目的只是做為內嵌在Browser中，製作動態效果的小語言，在2005年之前被認為只是業餘人士使用的簡易網頁工具，後來由於Ajax技術的提出、Node.js的成功、HTML5的普及、瀏覽器本身的進展，結合健全發展的函式庫生態系，在2006年之後至今，JavaScript逐漸發展成為可獨立執行且前後台通用的重要語言。然而JavaScript本身易物難精，由於基本身弱型別與不嚴格的語法檢查，加上進階構件如Prototype-based的物件導向設計、函式導向 (Functional)與非同步 (Asynchronous)等概念經常讓初學者難以理解，導致所開發的程式邏輯錯誤或不堪使用。AI的發展讓入門者也能具有初階工程師的程式能力，若有意在未來在工作中以JavaScript+AI協作者，對語言知識的深層理解會大幅拉開與入門者的差距。
本課程分為二階段，在前半將著重於講授JavaScript語言幾個自學者容易遇到瓶頸的概念，在這部份涉及語言機制與思維理解，所有作業與練習不可使用生成式AI; 後半則配合p5.js與相關函式庫介紹JavaScript如何運用於操作各式數位媒材，包含文字、互動、排版、圖片、動畫、音訊與影片，並設計數位創作，在第二階段將鼓勵學生活用生成式AI於程式設計，例如 OpenAI Codex或GitHub Copilot。
本課程不會重新講授基本程式概念，如變數、陣列、函式、流程控制(if-else)、迴圈，因此建議已修過至少一門程式設計(入門)課程，再修習本課程較為恰當，否則會跟不上課程的進度。
* 需自備筆電。

1. JavaScript程式語言結構與重要特性
2. 理解各式數位內容的特性與操作方式
3. 能基於所學資訊技術進行至少一項團體創作
4. 適當使用 OpenAI Codex、GitHub Copilot 等工具輔助程式設計與數位創作
5. 理解 AI 對軟體教育、軟體工程與產業的影響，並培養驗證、判斷及負責任使用 AI 的素養

課程簡介:
This course uses lectures and assignments to help students understand the interaction process between people and products, so that they can learn how to design the best possible interaction experiences with digital media. Here, "products" refers broadly to any object, digital content, or service in our environment.
The course consists of the following units:
The Nature of Interaction.
In all things interactive, interaction takes place through an "interface" defined by several core elements. Interacting through interfaces is one of the fundamental ways the world works. This unit takes an analytical approach to what various interface concepts have in common, how they form the basis of human-computer interaction, and how HCI concepts apply across a range of phenomena.
The Psychological Basis of HCI.
"Human" is at the core of HCI, but what does that really mean, and what constraints does it impose? What principles guide how people process information within interfaces and interactive processes? Starting with the visual system, this unit introduces perception, memory, cognition, and the laws of human factors engineering — and asks what "intuitive" actually means.
HCI and Communication.
This unit covers classical communication theory and the principles of human-to-human dialogue, showing how these principles underlie HCI and how they can be applied to understand the successes and failures of an interaction.
The Context of HCI and Design.
This unit introduces basic design-research methods and data presentation, and shows how data can deepen our understanding of both the user (human) and the function (machine).
Methods and Tools for Designing HCI.
This unit covers task design axes and goals, along with the design elements of human-computer interfaces — graphical interface elements and conventions, information visualization, perceptual design, and information architecture.
Prototyping and Evaluation of HCI Design.
A prototype is a tool for verification and optimization, and effective prototyping must go hand in hand with effective evaluation. This unit introduces a range of prototyping techniques and evaluation methods.
New HCI Technologies.
This unit covers the foundational technologies of the metaverse — Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) — and their impact on the future of HCI.
Note: This course will be taught in English by two faculty members: Prof. Yihsiu Chen (陳宜秀) for Weeks 1–8, and Prof. Tsung-yu Yoyo Ho (侯宗佑) for Weeks 9–16.
課程目標與學習成效:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the principles and applications of HCI as a foundation of digital media
Understand the structure, design process, and value of HCI
Apply course content to observe and make sense of everyday phenomena
Apply course content to professional design and production work
Recognize emerging interactive technologies and their possibilities for future development

課程簡介:
本課程雖以「創作」為名，但實際上並不會教「創作」本身，而是更偏向實作練習，讓同學在課程結束後，不會被技術限制，而能在創作上更加自由
本課程將以 Unity3D 作為主要的開發工具。雖然 Unity3D 經常被用於遊戲開發，但本課程的教材將以「非遊戲」的方式來進行設計，旨在拆解各項遊戲引擎中的元素，帶領各位實際操作「互動新媒體領域」經常使用到的觀念與技術，以期待同學們未來在實作上可以有更彈性的思考
—
本課程將會包含較廣泛的概念，除了 Unity3D 軟體本身的基礎操作概念以外，還會包含 3D 建模、動畫、動態演算法、Shader、API 呼叫等概念。授課時，比起仔細教導各項技術細節，本課程更傾向於讓同學掌握整體的概念，因為當代的 AI 技術已經成了最好的實作導師。只要同學具備正確的觀念理解，便可以藉由 AI 輕易的取得正確、可執行的程式碼，甚至架構概念清晰時，也可以在不調整程式碼的情況下進行完整的專案實作
因此，本課程的設計為，在上課時，同學可以帶著輕鬆的心情到教室，老師會以手把手的方式，帶同學走過一遍整個實作的過程，讓同學理解這項技術的實際用法為何。但若要能夠實際應用到自己的創作、實作中，則有賴同學在課後自行摸索練習。因此本課程的課程不需預習，也可帶著輕鬆的心情來課，但會需要花費較多時間進行課程後的練習實作
—
另外，在軟體開發中應用 AI 將會是未來的重要技能與趨勢，因此本課程將會高度鼓勵同學使用 AI。課程中會試著帶同學申請學生版的免費 AI 服務，但由於各公司政策經常有變，因此難以保證該免費服務足夠使用，也期待當課程中需要購買付費 AI 服務時，同學能以購入課本的心態來進行付費

數位技術：
理解如何使用 Unity3D 進行製作
廣泛理解各項「互動新媒體」中的技術概念

課程中會包含大量的創作練習，藉由大量的創作，來了解自身的創作能量

相對論：高速的世界與彎曲的時空
當物體接近光速時，時間會變慢，長度會縮短，呈現出奇幻的時空現象。一對雙胞胎在地球上原本同齡，其中一人搭乘太空船進行高速旅行，返航時發現自己依然年輕，而留在地球上的兄弟姊妹卻已經白髮蒼蒼。原因在於，假設當太空船以 0.8 倍光速飛行時，太空船上經過的三十年，地球上可能已經過了五十年。
另一方面，重力主導著日月星辰的運行，但我們將理解，重力並非傳統意義上的力，而是時空幾何的表現。質量告訴時空如何彎曲，時空告訴質量如何運動。
量子力學：顛覆直覺的微觀世界
在原子與基本粒子的尺度中，世界與日常經驗截然不同，量子事件以機率的方式被描述，並呈現出疊加與不確定性等特性。我們驚訝地發現，量子世界不再像古典物理那樣，只要知道系統的初始條件，就能根據物理定律精確預測未來。
粒子的能量是量子化的，對應不同的量子態。許多量子現象更是超乎我們的直覺：量子穿隧讓粒子有機會穿越古典物理中無法跨越的障礙；量子糾纏讓兩個粒子彷彿具有心電感應一般；量子疊加則是量子計算的核心。
我們將理解，量子力學居然與太陽的核融合、元素週期表與化學反應息息相關；而從半導體、雷射、核磁共振、電子顯微鏡到量子電腦，量子力學不僅改變了人類理解自然的方式，也深刻影響著現代科技。
課程目標與學習成效:
1.理解近代物理與古典物理的不同
2.訓練獨立思考的能力，提升自身科學素養，亦可作為之後專業課程的基礎。
3.學習近代物理學在多學科領域及科技發展中的應用。

課程簡介: 本課程旨在介紹計算思維與人工智慧的基本概念、原理和應用，為之後修習資訊相關課程奠下基礎。21世紀數位時代，如何具有應用人工智慧技術能力，培養計算思維是第一步，因為計算思維是分析問題、制定解決方法的思考過程，其中解決的步驟得依循電腦運算邏輯，因此在有了抽象思考能力後，將進一步介紹電腦具體運作架構，兩者的結合將由人工智慧程式應用來加以練習，此外也將介紹人工智慧的發展歷程和未來趨勢，以及人工智慧對社會、經濟和文化的影響。                                                                                                                                                                            This course aims to introduce fundamental concepts, principles, and applications of computational thinking and artificial intelligence, establishing a foundation for subsequent information technology-related coursework. In the 21st century digital era, developing computational thinking capabilities represents the essential first step toward effectively applying artificial intelligence technologies. Computational thinking encompasses the analytical processes for problem identification and solution formulation, wherein problem-solving procedures must adhere to computer operational logic. After developing abstract thinking skills, we will explore concrete computer operational architectures in more detail. The integration of these elements will be practiced through artificial intelligence programming applications. Additionally, we will investigate the developmental trajectory and future trends of artificial intelligence, and evaluate its impact on society, the economy, and culture.

This course aims to clarify the connotations of information technology in the digital world, the development of the internet world, and the challenges of big data in the digital world. It cultivates students' core competencies, including information technology knowledge, basic programming logic, interdisciplinary knowledge, self-reflection, and civic literacy. Furthermore, through final AI and sustainability projects, it enhances students' AI knowledge, sustainability literacy, communication skills, leadership, and teamwork abilities.

課程簡介:
本課程著重「如何使用 Python 程式語言，以人工神經網路架構，撰寫 AI 相關之應用軟體」，內容相當於坊間的「深度學習」課程。課程目標包含：如何利用人工神經網路，針對影像、以及人類使用的自然語言（如：英文、中文），進行特徵抽取後，找出其中的規律與趨勢，並加以運用至手寫辨識、人機對話等場合。
本課程特色為：全程使用「AI 模型」，來輔助您程式碼的撰寫。每一個單元會先講解一種神經網路模型背後的原理，讓您了解模型背後運作的流程。接著您就可以把流程，轉化為用白話文撰寫而成的「提詞」，要求 AI 產生您想要的神經網路程式碼。
課程中，會使用 Python 來撰寫程式。因此選修此課程的同學，必須對 Python 語言有一定的認識。包含分支、迴圈等基礎語法，Tuple, List, Dict 等資料結構，以及函數的設計與撰寫等。若對物件導向程式設計的製作熟悉者更佳。
由於神經網路非常倚賴「機率與統計」這門學問。所以課程講解過程中，難免會談論到「平均值、標準差、常態分佈」等名詞。雖講師會在授課過程中，提供簡單的說明，唯同學們仍須對統計學的一些基本名詞有所認識，以取得更好的學習成效。
完成課程後，您將熟悉下列神經網路模型：
(1) 基本人工神經網路（ANN, Artificial Neural Networks）：此乃一切神經網路的基礎模型。包含如何使用 Keras 套件，執行迴歸、分類等任務。
(2) 卷積神經網路（CNN, Convolutional Neural Networks），可以從影像自動抽取特徵，讓神經網路學會辨識照片裡的物體。
(3) 循環神經網路（RNN, Recurrent Neural Networks），能從人類日常使用的「自然語言」中，理解人類想要表達的意圖。其間會以 RNN，來辨識一則留言到底是「正評」還是「負評」，做為本小節的範例。
(4) 生成式神經網路（GNN, Generative Neural Network），包含如何用神經網路，生成各式圖片、文字之技術。包含「變分自動編碼器（Variational Autoencoder）」、「生成對抗網路（Generative Adversarial Networks, GAN）」、「擴散式模型（Diffusion Models）」等。
期待您學完本課程後，能對如何使用神經網路解決問題，有更深一層的認識。

1.理解資訊安全的重要性

課程目標與學習成效: 密碼學技術為區塊鏈的關鍵核心技術之一。比特幣利用雜湊函數(hash function)演算法來進行工作量證明。而ECDSA橢圓曲線數位簽章標準則用來確保交易的安全性與不可否認性。除此之外，密碼學亦是現代電子商務、網路安全等必備之工具。本課程將介紹密碼學的基本理論及其實務。基本理論將介紹公開金鑰密碼技術、數位簽章及電子認證的技術、秘密分享機制、橢圓曲線密碼、多方安全計算、零知識證明等密碼協定的設計與安全性分析。

課程簡介: 本課程介紹資訊理論與資料壓縮的基本概念，涵蓋資訊量、熵、編碼理論，以及無失真與有失真壓縮技術。課程內容包含 Huffman Coding、Arithmetic Coding、LZ-Coding、Predictive Coding、Transform Coding、Wavelet Coding，以及視訊壓縮等主題，並探討資訊理論在多媒體資料壓縮中的應用。透過理論講解、數值計算與案例分析，使學生理解各種壓縮技術背後的原理與設計理念，並培養分析與評估資料壓縮方法的能力。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程旨在介紹資訊理論與資料壓縮的基本概念與核心技術，使學生理解資訊量、熵、編碼效率與通道容量等資訊理論基礎，並進一步學習無失真與有失真壓縮技術之原理與應用。課程內容涵蓋多種編碼技巧以及視訊壓縮等主題，培養學生對多媒體資料壓縮方法的理解與分析能力。修習本課程後，學生應能計算資訊熵、平均碼長與編碼效率等相關指標，理解各類資料壓縮技術的設計原理與特性，分析不同壓縮方法在壓縮率、計算成本與資料品質之間的取捨，並能以資訊理論觀點探討多媒體資料壓縮技術於實際應用中的設計、限制與安全性相關議題。

本課程首先介紹工業物聯網及相關技術、發展趨勢，協助學生了解相關應用。接下來介紹工業物聯網之架構及元件，從感知、收集、傳輸、至處理，及相關協定與對應資安議題，讓學生具備工業物聯網全觀認知。課程接續介紹OT營運技術之資安架構、標準、並透過案例說明OT資安防護應用。課程另擬規劃國內工業物聯網相關企業參訪、以及業師共同授課，增進課程產學聯結並促進學生就業觀。

課程簡介:
国際関係理論と称する講義、著作は、米国だけでなく台湾、日本でも相当数にのぼる。
台湾の学生にとって身近な国際関係は、戦後最も緊密な関係を有した対米関係、あるいは最も身近な隣国である対日関係、そして、冷戦終結後に生まれた世代にとっては両岸関係も国際関係の範疇に属するとみなせるかもしれない。極論すれば、台湾にとって、最も重要な国際関係とは台米関係、両岸関係、台日関係であろう。
本講義は、社会科学的視点から日本研究を学ぶ台湾人学生を念頭において設計しており、具体的には、国際政治史と国際関係理論への知識の習得と応用においている。
はじめに、「国際政治学」、「国際関係理論」をリードしてきた欧米研究者の文献を読み、
20
世紀以降の国際政治の大きな流れを掌握し、リアリズム、リベラリズム等の代表的な理論や概念を理解し、国際関係の中で起きてきた事象を理解、分析する。
また日本（台湾）においては、「欧米の理論を直輸入し、紹介している」という批判を意識し、国際社会における日本の現状や日本の国際政治に対する問題意識を反映した視点を採りこむために、日本人研究者による文献を読み、日本の視点から国際関係への視角を概観する。
課程目標與學習成效:
講義で使用する文献を読むことによって、以下の成果が上がるよう目標とする。
１．
20
世紀以降の国際政治の大きな流れを習得する。その際に、その時の台湾、日本はいかなる存在であったのかということを常に意識する。
２．現代国際関係理論におけるパラダイムであるリアリズム、リベラリズム、コンストラクトヴィズムのほか、主要分析レベル（国家、個人、国際システム）の概念を理解する。
３．既存の理論、視角を通じて日本と特定の国家、あるいは日本の行為を分析する。大学院における講義における一般的な目標としては、実証的な日本研究をするための基盤を整えるとともに、明確な問題意識を持ち、仮説を立て、分析するという流れの習得も目指す。
４．課外学習　政府機関などを訪問して実務的現場に触れる。

課程目標與學習成效:
在學術的研究中，常見的研究題目的類型主要有詮釋型、探索型、描述型、解釋型以及評估型這幾種，這一堂課的主要目的是指導同學們該如何對「描述型」（descriptive）、「解釋型」（explanatory）以及「評估型」（evaluative）這三種題目進行「社會科學」的「實證研究」，並且培養同學們學術論文寫作與發表的基本技巧。
本課程主要涵蓋三大部分的內容：第一個部分是關於如何作一個「科學的」研究，包括如何尋找因果關係、如何透過文獻形成研究問題、如何透過文獻建構一個「可以在經驗上被否證的」理論（theory）或是論點（argument），以及如何透過研究設計（research design）來檢證因果關係（也就是你所建構的理論或是論點所聲稱的內容）；第二個部分為一些常見的主要研究方法，研究者可根據「是否可以進行實驗」、「案例數目的多寡」以及「分析單位」這三個標準，來選擇其中的一種或多種研究方法在研究中使用，其背後共享的邏輯為「如何在各種不同的情況之下盡可能地逼近『實驗法』的研究設計」，以及「如何讓你的研究設計有辦法被其他的研究者進行複證」；第三個部分則是關於論文寫作與發表的技巧，包括論文的基本格式、引用文獻的格式與方法、論述的過程、一些常犯錯誤的避免，以及如何對自己與別人的研究做出專業的發表和評論。由於我們俄研所和日本學程注重的是對俄國和日本的黨政、經濟、社會與外交等相關問題的研究，因此在研究問題的性質上，「比較研究法」（comparative method）與「個案研究法」（case study method）很可能會是各位同學們所必須採用的主要研究方法（為什麼呢？），因此本課程也將在各週提及這兩個研究方法如何與各週的主題相輔相成。
在課程進行的過程中，同學們將分段完成自己的期末研究論文計劃的各個重要部分，並且將在期末在課堂上舉辦一個模擬學術研討會，由同學們分別擔任主持人、發表人、評論人與聽眾，培養進行學術研究與發表的專業能力。
同學們應可在課程中發現，社會科學的實證研究基本上就是一連串你如何去justify「你如何發現問題」與「你如何解決問題」的過程，這個方法論與研究設計的訓練，除了對同學們的研究與寫作有幫助之外，對於我們思考每天的社會現象與日常生活中的切身問題也都會帶來很多的啟發。

課程簡介:
日本古典文法是一套和現代日文大不相同的文法體系，卻又是現代日文的根源與先驅。現存日文的相關資料中，除了日本古典文學等領域之外，台灣殖民文學、近現代日本文學、台日政治史等相關文獻，甚至是日本媒體廣告、動漫中，也存在著為數不少的古典文法。因此培養解讀日本古文的能力，不僅是有助於學習者理解日語文法體系的歷史脈絡、掌握日語的特色，更是進行日本研究、理解日本文化時的重要先行工作。本課程分上下學期，欲修下學期課程者，請務必修上學期課程。

課程簡介:
本課程旨在從國際安全、國防政策與軍事戰略的整合視角，分析日本軍事力量的歷史演變、制度轉型與戰力建構。
課程首先說明戰後和平憲法、專守防衛原則及日美安全體制，探討日本自衛隊如何在法律限制、國內政治與區域安全環境交互下逐步發展；並分析日本《國家安全保障戰略》、《國家防衛戰略》及《防衛力整備計畫》等國安三文件，掌握日本由本土防衛轉向跨域整合、機動部署、反擊能力與聯盟協同的戰略變化。
在戰力建構方面，課程將檢視陸上、海上及航空自衛隊的兵力結構、指揮體系、主要裝備與作戰任務，並討論飛彈防禦、遠程精準打擊、反潛作戰、兩棲機動、太空、網路、電磁頻譜及無人系統等新興能力。同時分析日本國防科技、軍工產業、武器出口、供應鏈安全及國際共同研發對防衛自主的影響。
此外，本課程將日本軍事發展置於美中戰略競爭、朝鮮半島、俄羅斯遠東活動及台海安全脈絡中，評估日美同盟及多邊安全合作對日本戰略角色的塑造。透過政策文件研讀、案例分析與情境推演，培養學生分析軍事力量建構、國防資源配置及印太安全變化的能力。

一、講義の説明（課程簡介）
台湾にとって日本は、
1972

課程簡介:
The world is changing faster than our maps of it. Hegemonic competition now spans chips and shipping lanes; wars are redrawing borders in Europe and the Middle East; great-power rivalries stretch across the Indo-Pacific and Asia-Pacific regions; artificial intelligence advances by the month; and the climate system is breaching thresholds once thought to be decades away. We now live in a world of unknowns, where yesterday’s certainties expire before the semester ends. In such a world, no subject is more critical than International Relations: it is the discipline that asks why states fight or cooperate, why international orders rise and unravel, and how power, ideas, and institutions shape the fates of nations—and of all of us who live in them. This course might not offer you predictions. But it will attempt something more durable: to equip you with the theories and analytical tools needed to ask better questions of a world that refuses to stand still.
Against this backdrop, this graduate seminar is intended to provide an advanced introduction to the major theoretical traditions, analytical approaches, contemporary problems, and emerging frontiers in International Relations (IR). As a seminar, the course expects each student to complete the assigned readings before coming to class and to participate actively in course discussions and simulation activities.
Rather than organizing the course exclusively around the traditional “isms,” the course proceeds in four stages. Part I (Long-Standing Foundational Paradigms) examines the foundational theoretical traditions of IR, including realism, liberalism, institutionalism, constructivism, critical approaches, and psychological and behavioral extensions. Part II (New Analytical Perspectives) turns to the analytical toolkits that reoriented the field around domestic politics and strategic interaction, as well as to theorizing from outside the great powers. Part III (Critical Phenomena in Modern International Relations) applies theory to the central empirical problems of contemporary world politics: war and political violence, the global economy, energy, and geopolitical and economic competition. Part IV (New Frontiers: Challenges of the Anthropocene) confronts the planetary and technological transformations—climate change and migration, emerging technologies, and artificial intelligence—that test the limits of inherited IR theory. The course will also feature invited talks, which will be announced later in the semester.
Throughout the course, students will be asked to identify the assumptions, causal mechanisms, scope conditions, and empirical implications of competing theories. The aim is to encourage students to read critically, participate actively, connect theory to evidence, and design original research.
課程目標與學習成效:
Master the core concepts, debates, and theories of contemporary IR.
Identify the principal actors, mechanisms, and international dimensions of each substantive area.
Apply IR theory to analyze current international developments.
Design and write an original, theoretically grounded research paper.

課程簡介: This course examines the political economy of East Asia’s remarkable transformation from a relatively poor and war-torn region into one of the central engines of the global economy. It explores how states, markets, and societies have interacted to shape distinctive development trajectories across Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, China, and Southeast Asia, and how these experiences challenge orthodox theories of development and globalization.
課程目標與學習成效:
Beginning with classic debates on the developmental state and regional production hierarchies, the course traces the rise, evolution, and diversification of state-led development models in East Asia. It compares democratic and authoritarian variants of developmentalism, analyzes China’s economic rise and its integration into the global political economy, and assesses how late developers have navigated industrialization, globalization, and institutional change. Attention is given to trade and production networks, financial and currency cooperation, urban transformation, and the role of cities as global economic hubs.
The final part of the course focuses on contemporary challenges, including economic statecraft, geoeconomic competition, technological rivalry, and the growing fusion of economic and security concerns. By the end of the course, students will be able to critically evaluate competing explanations of East Asian development, understand variation across national cases, and assess how East Asia’s political economies are reshaping the global economic order.

課程簡介:
The course “
Protest, Conflict, and War: Contentious Politics and Violence in Southeast Asia”
straddles
International Studies, Political Science, and Political Sociology
, engaging with key debates on contentious politics and political violence through an interdisciplinary lens. It draws on foundational scholars such as Charles Tilly and Sidney Tarrow on contentious politics, Sidney Tarrow on social movements, James C. Scott on state power and resistance, Karl Marx on structural inequality, Henri Tajfel on social identity, René Girard on mimetic desire and scapegoating, Stathis Kalyvas on civil war violence, and Martha Crenshaw on terrorism. In doing so, the course examines how protest, conflict, violence, and war are interconnected processes rather than discrete phenomena.
The course is designed for graduate students in International Studies broadly
, where increasing attention to political instability, identity conflict, and violence requires stronger integration between political sociology, comparative politics, and international relations. It speaks directly to the need for analytically rigorous frameworks capable of explaining how collective action escalates across different political contexts, from everyday protest to organized armed conflict.
Within the
International Master’s Program in International Studies (IMPIS – NCCU),
this course enriches and extends the existing Southeast Asia-focused curriculum
by offering a more systematic and theoretically integrated treatment of contentious politics in the region. It complements existing courses such as
Hybrid Regimes: Democratic Challenges in Southeast Asia
,
Civil and Uncivil Societies in Southeast Asia
,
Ethnicity, Religion, Nationalism: Violence and the Politics of Belonging in the Global World
, and
Religion and Politics in the Modern World
, forming part of a coherent intellectual cluster on political order, identity, and conflict.
The course is structured in two parts. The first half develops theoretical foundations in contentious politics and theories of conflict and violence, applied through illustrative cases from Indonesia, Myanmar, Thailand, and the Philippines. The second half functions as a Southeast Asia laboratory, in which these frameworks are tested and refined through deeper comparative engagement with these four cases, alongside selected references to Cambodia and Timor-Leste where relevant to post-conflict trajectories and state formation dynamics.
課程目標與學習成效:
This course is grounded in interdisciplinary literatures from political sociology, comparative politics, and international relations, and is designed to equip students with conceptual, theoretical, and empirical tools for analyzing contentious political phenomena. It brings together scholarship on contentious politics (Tilly, Tarrow), structural inequality (Marx, Scott), identity formation (Tajfel, Horowitz), psychological and cultural theories of conflict escalation (Girard, Atran), political violence (Kalyvas, Brass), and terrorism studies (Crenshaw, Hoffman), with sustained empirical engagement in Southeast Asia.
At the end of the course, students will be able to critically analyze the dynamics of protest, conflict, violence, and war using multiple theoretical frameworks; compare escalation trajectories across Southeast Asian cases; evaluate the strengths and limitations of competing explanations of political violence; and apply interdisciplinary concepts to contemporary empirical developments in the region. Students will also develop the ability to synthesize theoretical and empirical materials into coherent analytical arguments appropriate for graduate-level research in International Studies.

選課設定_限制與加簽: 開放低年級: 是 Yes｜非本院名額: 15｜總名額: 15｜開放加簽: 是 Yes
課程簡介:
This seminar examines the political processes through which the contemporary international monetary and financial system is constructed and operated, and how national security relationships are intertwined with the international and monetary relationships. It introduces the theoretical frameworks and the empirical literature that allow students to analyze the major issues of international monetary, financial and security politics, and it supports students in developing an original research project of their own.
Few would deny that the integration of international monetary and financial markets is among the most consequential features of globalization. Susan Strange saw early that international relations and foreign policy would be increasingly constrained by monetary and financial affairs. Today firms and individuals can invest in, or withdraw from, distant economies almost instantaneously. High capital mobility has reshaped national economic policy and social order, and has unsettled the territorially bounded relationship between state, market and society. The systemic risks generated by financial globalization — the crisis of 2007–08 above all — have shaken established paradigms of national and global governance, and the anti-globalization backlash, protectionism, and trade and currency conflict that followed have become principal drivers of power transition and order change.
The seminar is organized in five parts. Part I introduces the core analytical problem — the ‘unholy trinity’ of exchange rate stability, capital mobility and national policy autonomy — together with the classical IPE paradigms, Open Economy Politics, constructivist and Everyday IPE, and the “securitization of geoecnomic/geopolitical economy” turn of the past few years. It then traces the historical construction of the modern order: the gold standard, the Great Depression and the Second World War; the rise and collapse of Bretton Woods; and the globalization of financial risk.
Part II turns to international monetary relations: the politics of exchange rate policy, the operation and limits of central banks, monetary regionalism, and international monetary power and currency statecraft. Part III addresses the international financial system: capital account liberalization and re-regulation, financial and sovereign debt crises and their governance, private authority and inequality in financial markets, and the challenge of digital money.
Part IV is new to this iteration of the seminar and takes up two developments that have moved to the centre of the field since the syllabus was last taught. The first is artificial intelligence: compute, semiconductors and data centres have become chokepoints in the global economy, AI is reshaping asset management and financial governance, and states are responding by building techno-blocs. The second is resilience and economic security: investment screening, export controls and supply-chain de-risking are now instruments of monetary and financial statecraft, and ‘resilience’ has become a governing category with its own distributive politics.
Part V concludes with the security implications of money and finance. As Cicero observed, the sinews of war are infinite money. International monetary relations and financial systems have always been bound up with military power, and this connection is now among the most active research frontiers in the field. We examine war finance, rearmament, and the relationship between financial capacity and power transition.
There are no prerequisites. Students who have not previously taken a seminar in international political economy can keep pace by completing the weekly readings, participating in discussion, and fulfilling the written requirements. Questions and requests for supplementary material are welcome in class, during office hours, or by email.
** NoteThis course is a highly intensive, research-focused seminar. The goal of this course is to help each registered student complete a publishable project related to the themes of the course by the end of the semester. Students who took this course are expected to develop a clear research topic and be prepared to immerse themselves in a substantial amount of IPE literature.
.
課程目標與學習成效:
By the end of the course, registered students are expected to have the following competencies:
1. be familiar with the political processes that underlie the construction and functioning of international monetary relations and the financial system, and understand the key issues affecting the governance of international money and finance, such as the Unholy Trinity, exchange rate stability, capital mobility, and national policy autonomy, as well as other important themes such as financial crises, monetary power, and monetary regionalism.
2. understand the key actors, modes of interaction, and international dimensions of each theme
3. apply the theories learnt in this course to explain the politics of international money and finance from the perspective of international political economy
4. design and write original, published research papers.

The course “Ethnicity, Religion, Nationalism: Violence and the Politics of Belonging in the Global World” provides a structured space for students to critically examine how ethnic and religious identities shape nationalism and contribute to political conflict and violence in different regional and international contexts.
The course explores the interaction between religion and ethnic identities in Asia (East Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia), the Middle East, and the United States, and their impact on the construction of nationalism. The course “Hybrid Regimes: Democratic Challenges in Southeast Asia” is designed as a standalone course or as a follow-up course for students who have completed the introductory course “Politics in Southeast Asia: Change and Continuity”. The course examines the socio-political development of authoritarian and hybrid regimes in Asia, enabling students to survey, compare, and analyze the persistent challenges of democratization in the region. While the empirical focus is Southeast Asia, the course also situates regional political dynamics within broader geopolitical relations, particularly with East Asian actors such as China, Taiwan, and Japan. Cambodia’s limited democratization, for instance, has been analyzed by some scholars in relation to its close ties with China. From this perspective, democratization in Southeast Asia may also be influenced by engagement with consolidated democracies, such as Taiwan and Japan.
The course further engages with Taiwan’s foreign policy initiative, the NEW SOUTHBOUND POLICY, through which Taiwan seeks to deepen economic, political, and cultural relations with Southeast Asian countries.
In the aftermath of the Cold War, a global wave of democratization reshaped political systems across Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, and Sub-Saharan Africa. The dissolution of the Soviet Union weakened the legitimacy of many authoritarian regimes, leading to transitions toward multiparty systems and liberal reforms. However, regime transitions did not always result in democratic consolidation, and many states experienced stalled or reversed democratization processes.
While pure authoritarian regimes have become less common in Asia, many states are better understood as “hybrid regimes” or “electoral autocracies”, positioned between liberal democracy and authoritarian rule. These regimes typically maintain the formal structures of electoral competition, including multiparty elections, while systematically limiting opposition voices through institutional manipulation, uneven political competition, and selective enforcement of rules. In these nations, the thin veneer of quasi-democratic institutions and multi-party elections became a façade for abuses of power, manipulation and corruption. In Thailand, following the 2019 election, the military-backed government dissolved an opposition party and arrested activists, triggering widespread student-led protests demanding constitutional reform and greater civil liberties. In 2023, although the opposition Move Forward Party won the election, it was prevented from forming a government due to institutional constraints and entrenched political interests. In the Philippines in 2016, voter dissatisfaction with crime and entrenched elite politics contributed to the election of Rodrigo Duterte, whose administration was associated with an extensive “war on drugs” involving extrajudicial killings. In 2022, voters elected Ferdinand Marcos Jr., the son and namesake of the former dictator, signaling the persistence of dynastic politics. In Myanmar, the military coup in 2021 marked a reversal of electoral democratization and a return to direct military rule.
The course also incorporates analysis of the role of digital technologies in shaping political competition and state-society relations in Southeast Asia
.
Social media platforms have become central arenas for electoral mobilization, political communication, and contestation in hybrid regimes.
Emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), further amplify these dynamics by enabling new forms of political communication and information manipulation at scale.
In several cases, coordinated online networks, including troll activities and disinformation campaigns, were deployed during election periods to influence public opinion and delegitimize opposition actors. Concurrently,
states have introduced regulatory frameworks such as anti-fake news legislation and cybersecurity laws, which, while formally justified in terms of public order and information integrity, may also function as instruments of digital surveillance
and constraints on freedom of expression. These developments underscore how hybrid regimes are sustained not only through formal institutions and coercive mechanisms, but also through digital infrastructures and information environments.
Some of the questions the course seeks to answer are: What is democracy good for? Why do some states democratize while others continue to exhibit authoritarianism? How do highly corrupt political regimes survive for decades? How do populist leaders gain and maintain power in Asia? What is the legacy of political violence in newly democratic states? What is the legacy of military rule in the region? How do global human rights values and “Asian values” shape political development in the region? How do digital technologies, including social media platforms, disinformation networks, and state regulatory frameworks, reshape political competition, state-society relations, and the boundaries of free expression in hybrid regimes? The course begins by introducing core concepts, regime typologies, and indicators for assessing democratization. It subsequently examines in-depth developments in Thailand, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Myanmar, Vietnam, and Cambodia.

本課程旨在從國際安全、國防政策與軍事戰略的整合視角，分析日本軍事力量的歷史演變、制度轉型與戰力建構。

課程簡介:
STEAM 為 Science、Technology、Engineering、Arts、Mathematics 的縮寫，強調科學、科技、工程、藝術與數學之間的跨領域整合。其發展背景與美國自 1980 年代以來對科學、科技與工程人才培育的政策關注密切相關；1990 年代以後，STEM／STEAM 教育更逐漸成為各國推動未來人才培育、創新能力與問題解決能力的重要教育取向。
然而，什麼是 STEAM 教育？STEAM 是否只是將科學、科技、工程、藝術與數學放在同一門課程中？其教育理念的核心價值與教學實踐方式又是什麼？有別於一般課程直接導入既有的 STEAM 教學活動或操作模式，本課程將先從科技與社會研究，亦即 STS（Science, Technology and Society）的角度出發，引導學生回溯 STEAM 教育形成的社會、科技與教育脈絡，理解其背後所回應的人才培育、社會變遷與知識整合需求。
在此基礎上，本課程將透過 STEAM 課程案例分析、實作示範、教學演練與課程設計，引導學生從親身體驗中理解 STEAM 教育的核心精神。課程不僅重視跨領域知識的整合，也強調真實問題情境、動手實作、創意思考、合作學習與反思表達。學生將在課程中共同討論 STEAM 教育的教育價值，並逐步建構基礎的 STEAM 教學設計、課程發展與實作引導能力。
本課程期望協助學生不只是認識 STEAM 的概念，更能理解 STEAM 教育如何作為一種回應科技社會變遷的教育實踐，進而培養未來在教學現場、教育推廣或跨領域學習活動中設計與實施 STEAM 課程的基礎能力。
課程目標與學習成效:
本課程旨在協助學生理解 STEAM 教育的發展脈絡、教育理念與實務操作方法，並透過科技與社會研究（STS）的觀點，引導學生思考 STEAM 教育如何回應科技發展、社會變遷與未來人才培育的需求。課程將結合理論介紹、案例分析、實作示範、教學演練與課程設計，使學生能逐步建立 STEAM 教育的基礎認識，並具備初步設計與實施 STEAM 課程活動的能力。
本課程之課程目標如下：
一、協助學生了解 STEAM 教育的發展脈絡，並建立對 Science、Technology、Engineering、Arts、Mathematics 跨領域整合教育的基礎認識。
二、引導學生從科技與社會研究（STS）的觀點，理解 STEAM 教育與科技發展、社會需求、產業變遷及人才培育之間的關係。
三、協助學生掌握 STEAM 教學的基本理念、原理原則與教學設計取向，包括問題導向、探究學習、動手實作、跨域整合、創意思考與合作學習。
四、透過 STEAM 課程案例分析，使學生理解不同 STEAM 教學模式的設計邏輯、課程結構與學習活動安排。
五、透過實作示範與教學演練，使學生親身體驗 STEAM 學習活動，並從過程中體認 STEAM 教育的核心價值。
六、培養學生將科學、科技、工程、藝術與數學元素整合為課程活動的能力，並能思考各領域知識在真實問題情境中的連結方式。
七、培養學生進行 STEAM 課程活動設計的能力，包括學習目標設定、活動流程規劃、材料與工具選擇、學習任務設計與成果呈現方式安排。
八、協助學生認識 Micro:bit 與基礎物聯網程式設計，理解感測器、輸入輸出、事件控制與簡易互動裝置在 STEAM 教育中的應用。
九、培養學生在 STEAM 教學活動中進行觀察、討論、反思與修正的能力，理解實作活動不只是完成作品，更包含問題理解、嘗試修正與學習表達。
十、培養學生具備初步的 STEAM 教育推廣、教學設計與跨領域課程發展能力。
學生修習本課程後，預期能具備以下學習成效：
一、能說明 STEAM 教育的基本意涵、發展背景與教育目的。
二、能區分 STEM 與 STEAM 教育的差異，並理解藝術、人文與創意元素在 STEAM 教育中的角色。
三、能從 STS 的角度說明科技、社會與教育之間的互動關係，並理解 STEAM 教育所回應的社會與人才培育需求。
四、能說明 STEAM 教學常見的原理原則，包括跨領域整合、真實問題情境、探究學習、設計思考、動手實作、合作學習與反思表達。
五、能分析 STEAM 課程案例中的學習目標、活動流程、跨領域元素、教學策略與學習成效。
六、能參與 STEAM 實作活動，並從實作過程中理解問題發現、構想形成、原型製作、測試修正與成果分享的學習歷程。
七、能運用基礎教學設計概念，規劃一個適合特定學習對象的 STEAM 課程活動或教案雛形。
八、能將科學、科技、工程、藝術與數學中的至少兩個以上領域元素整合到課程活動設計中。
九、能使用 Micro:bit 進行基礎互動設計，理解按鈕、LED 顯示、感測器、條件判斷與事件控制等基本概念。
十、能說明 Micro:bit 與物聯網基礎概念如何應用於 STEAM 教學活動，例如環境感測、互動裝置、資料蒐集或創意作品設計。
十一、能透過小組合作完成 STEAM 活動設計、實作演練或成果發表，並清楚表達設計理念與教學目標。
十二、能針對 STEAM 課程活動進行反思，指出活動中的優點、限制、學生可能遇到的學習困難，以及後續可修正之方向。

課程簡介:
The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which was adopted by the United Nations in 2015, has become a shared blueprint for peace and well-being of all human beings and the planet. Education, either as a goal and a means for achieving the global goal for sustainable development, has been given special attention by both global and local society.
This subject provides a platform for participants to understand and reconsider the relationship between education and sustainable development goals in East Asia. It starts with an introduction to the basic knowledge of sustainable development goals (SDGs) for a more balanced development of the world by 2030. Then, it moves to discuss about the educational perspectives of the SDGs in the context of East Asia. In the third part of the subject, it gives focus on achievement and challenges of education and SDGs in Japan’s context. It closes by making group presentations on how to frame a new social contract for futures of education in/for SDGs in the Asia-Pacific region by participants.
課程目標與學習成效:
Objectives of this subject are to enable students to:
1. obtain knowledge of sustainable development goals for the global society by 2030.
2. have a more comprehensive and more in-depth understanding of the relationship between education and sustainable development in the global community and the context of East Asia.
3. reconsider critically about the current policies and practices of education in/for sustainable development in East Asia.
4. raise a blueprint to frame a new social contract for education and development in/for SDGs in Asia-Pacific region.

課程簡介: Research Methods in Counseling is a sophisticated graduate-level course that emphasizes deeply on the principles, theories, and practices of counseling, along with incorporating advanced research methods. The course seeks to cultivate an enriched understanding of the therapeutic relationship, the dynamics of human behavior, and the transformative power of counseling interventions. The focus is prominently on the core counseling principles such as empathy, unconditional positive regard, active listening, and ethical considerations in professional practice. Students will delve into diverse counseling theories and models that guide therapeutic interventions and explore their application in various counseling settings like schools and families. The integration of these principles with research methods is meticulously addressed to ensure students are adept at applying theoretical knowledge and practical skills in real-world counseling scenarios, fostering professional growth and development in the counseling field. The amalgamation of counseling principles with research methods in this course aims to create a nuanced, holistic perspective on counseling practices.
課程目標與學習成效:
To equip students with an integrated knowledge of research methods and counseling principles, enabling them to design, conduct, critique, and apply research in practical counseling scenarios effectively.
▪ understand the strengths, weaknesses, and challenges of various research methods.
▪ choose and design appropriate research methods for their own research.
▪ critique others’ research in terms of their methodologies.
▪ develop a holistic understanding and application of advanced counseling principles and theories in diverse counseling settings.
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Synthesize and Apply Integrated Knowledge:
Understand and employ a comprehensive integration of counseling theories, principles, and models to demonstrate a holistic understanding of diverse counseling practices.
Develop and Implement Therapeutic Interventions:
Design and apply ethical and effective therapeutic interventions, using varied counseling theories and models to address the transformative power of counseling and human behavior dynamics.
Design, Conduct, and Evaluate Ethical Research:
Design, conduct, and critically evaluate robust and ethical research projects, incorporating advanced methodologies to assess and resolve complex counseling scenarios.
Critique Research and Counseling Approaches:
Critically analyze and appraise the applicability and efficacy of various research and counseling methodologies, demonstrating theoretical and ethical discernment in professional practice.
Demonstrate Ethical Sensitivity and Multicultural Competency:
Exhibit ongoing professional development, ethical sensitivity, and multicultural competency in applying counseling principles and research methods in real-world scenarios.

課程簡介: 早在以生活於中原地區漢族為主的華夏文化初期，「經」的重要性已被明確指出。《莊子‧天下》即明言：「《詩》以道志，《書》以道事，《禮》以道行，《樂》以道和，《易》以道陰陽，《春秋》以道名分。其數散於天下而設於中國者，百家之學時或稱而道之」，可知「經」所產生的影響，不單止於儒家內部。且其意義涉及自我修身、倫理實踐、宇宙存有等面向，舉凡生而在世所面對的諸般問題，經典都有所回應。經典不僅有自身傳承的譜系，延綿不絕；亦有應世運用的表現，這都成為學習儒家經典，探討經學發展的重要內涵。這也將是本課程的主要內容。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程從「傳經」、「解經」、「用經」三個面向，介紹儒家經學發展歷程。通過本課程，期使修習者對影響古代文化深遠的經學整體發展概況、各階段的特徵重心，有所掌握。進而由事見理，反思何謂經典與經學。

課程目標與學習成效: 本課程旨在介紹中國道教與其所開展出文化傳統，帶領同學認識道化文學的諸般面向及其內涵，培養相關的文本閱讀與分析能力。中國道教文化範圍甚廣，涵括了文學（遊仙詩、度脫劇、仙境與神魔小說）、經典（天師道、上清、靈寶、神霄、丹道）、儀式、圖象等等，範圍甚廣，由於時間所限，同時配合學生教學需求，本課程擬從「前道教時期的巫系文學傳統」、「道教文學」、「道教諸神與法術」三大面向介紹，討論其中所牽涉的道教觀念、義涵及內容主題，尤其希望集中最為民眾熟知的道教神祇與法術這兩項主題，討論它在各式題材中的表現與意義。閱讀材料包括了前道教時期的楚辭、六朝與唐代的遊仙詩與仙境小說、道教經典、神仙聖傳與筆記小說等。整體來說，本課程由道教內部出發，試圖引領同學思考道教文化開展出哪些主題或傳統，以及如何由道教出發，加深相關作品的理解與詮釋，同時希望由小見大，可以延伸到中國宗教文化研究，以此豐富同學對中國文化傳統的認識。

課程簡介:
在不斷全球化與數位化的影響下，川端康成、大江健三郎、高行健、莫言以「極具」亞洲風格的作品走向了諾貝爾，走到了全世界文學愛好者的心中。成為了諾貝爾得獎當年度「在文學領域創作出具理想傾向之最佳作品者」，評審評價他們以非凡的敏銳、刻骨銘心的洞察力和語言的豐富睿智性，呈現出了作品的張力，更認定後兩者為中文小說拉開了新的道路，認為民間故事、歷史和現代通過其文本敘述融為了一體。然而評審的所見，是否也是所有人的感受？他們是否就能代表亞洲，或者中文世界呢？還是在當今體系中，我們都只是看
/
被看之間的關係，就如同中文與海外華文文學之間的聯繫？我們在同一個世界裡，在不同的時空中說著相似或者相反的話語？
如果要解答上述問題，那麼我們就一定要認識海外華文文學，海外華文文學發展至今日，是一個特殊的存在，它源自於中文語系，演變自今日卻擁有一片「自己的」獨特天空。這堂概論課，將會對文學、語言的歸屬問題進行討論、解析，同時會從作品出發探討作品背後深層的意義。將與文學有關的因素如作品題材的選取、時空地域、政治經濟文化等綜合一起作語境考量。從第一代海外作者共同經歷離散和客居的煎熬，生存在多種文化衝擊的夾縫之中，親身體會到疏離和同化之間的掙扎，以所在的異地文化地理，用長距離鏡頭對原鄉的文化進行「客居式」的嚮往、勾勒式的描繪開始。到第二代海外作者在異鄉落地深耕，有別於第一代的「鄉愁」，產生「在地人」的意識根本變化，單一的觀察視角逐漸轉成多元的視角，以及現在的第三代和海外漢學家們並置呈現出一片豐富的萬物眾生相，從「風景的發現」到「風景的製造」，從中心的本位思想到去中心化的轉變，逐步形成自己的看法，從不同的角度重新認識中文世界。
本課程面向國教碩一、碩二同學，相對於大學部的華文文學概論的概念式講解，碩士主要集中於背後生成的意義與探討，以專題的形式對碩士生形成有效的理論脈絡，建構海外華文文學視野，使之將來能運用到論文寫作中。

課程簡介:
書
目療法（Bibliotherapy）向來見於圖書館系所或教育院所之課程，以及醫療照護院所之實務中。但實際上，「書目療法」是實踐於專業與日常生活中的應用實務。本課程在發展性的取向（Developmental approach）原則下，除心理勵志之自助文本外，本課程更著重在創意式文學文本之書目療法應用；並藉由閱讀理論與認知行為治療（CBT）做為書目療法立論依據，內容論及書目療法歷史發展，而與閱讀指導、圖書館讀者顧問服務、西方文學經典敘事應用、存在主義心理學與哲學、情緒療癒與基督教靈修等議題有關。由於課程同時著重於相關理論建置與書目解題介紹，以及創新的「自助式與創意式」解題書目的編製與討論，並引導學生如何進行相關主題之研究寫作，因而對於一般個人、閱讀推廣教師、圖書資訊服務以及讀者/閱讀理論等議題之深度探討亦有所助益。此課程著重於理論研究，但也藉由實務應用以激發學習者興趣和領悟。期待在閱讀與學習統整過程中，從啟發而鼓舞，進而使內心平安喜樂，這便是書目療法帶來的美善力量。
課程目標與學習成效:
認識「書目療法」的意義與精神，使學習者能藉由課程認同閱讀的價值和良善；
認識「書目療法」之閱讀推廣精要，使學習者在選擇「虛構與非虛構文本」與心理自助書籍時，能具備良好思辨能力；
認識CBT之敘事與類比等技巧來掌握文學作品對於書目療法的助益，並教導圖書選題；以及如何創新解題書目內容編製，加添蘇格拉底式提問要件，以做為讀者諮詢顧問服務之整備；
略以延伸「聖經書目療法」與若干經典文學作品之內涵與意義，使學習者能夠掌握課程所挑選設計之書目中，從中感受經典文學與各類型文本媒材之美，並學習到如何從認同、淨化、領悟三個傳統步驟中，進階至認同、勸慰、淨化、領悟之四階段論。就此反思如何藉由閱讀走出心靈困頓，以提升圖書資訊服務的延伸職能；
本課程涉及基督教經典與神學論點，同學仍可經由自身宗教信仰與觀點進入書目療法的學習與解題技巧之實務應用。

課程簡介: 本課程由數位人文與數位策展兩個環節所組成。數位人文強調開發數位資源內容的方法，數位策展則著重於將運用數位人文所開發的資源內容，運用多元形式進行呈現；兩者之間有其因果關係，也可促使學生更進一步說出數位資源內容的「故事」。在數位人文部份，本課程將引介文字探勘、語料庫分析、社會網絡分析等多面向方法，使學生有能力處理不同類型的數位資源，引導學生從詞彙、人物關聯的角度妥善分析數位資源內容；除展示各種數位人文技術的工具與應用範例外，更期盼運用各項數位人文的實作，引導學生探索數位科技如何影響並豐富學習內涵。在數位策展部份，本課程則從資料視覺化、地理資訊系統的角度，向學生介紹如何運用前述概念強化數位敘事的能力，進一步豐富數位策展的呈現，以開展跨領域學習興趣。
課程目標與學習成效:
理解數位人文與數位策展的核心概念，描述數位人文與數位策展的基本定義、應用範疇及其相互關係。
使用文字探勘與語料庫分析的方法，進行數位資源的詞彙標註、情緒分析和語料庫建構，以掌握文字探勘與語料庫分析技術。
利用社會網絡分析工具，提取文本中的人物關係，並辨別關係網絡中的重要人物或群體，使學生能應用社會網絡分析於數位資源研究。
描述數位典藏的發展歷史與發展，以及實體資源數位化的流程與優勢，以便了解數位典藏的步驟與流程。
熟悉資料視覺化技術及其應用，使學生能妥善使用資料視覺化工具，將數據轉化為視覺化圖像，增強數位策展的呈現效果。
理解地理資訊系統的基本概念，並將其應用於數位策展，進行地理資料的詞彙萃取與視覺化呈現。
理解遊戲化機制的概念，並應用於數位策展，學習如何通過遊戲化平台，提升資料內容與使用者的互動性與參與感。
促進人文與數位領域的合作，使學生能夠整合數位技術和人文學科的知識，培養綜合性的跨域思維。

計量模型會因分析資料的型態、特質、或研究的課題之不同有所差異。例如，橫斷面資料、追蹤資料、截斷資料、質量資料、期間資料、時間序列資料、空間資料等等之資料型態；與連續變數、選擇變數、計數資料、順序變數、間斷變數等等之資料特質。因此，本課程之授課內容將先講解統計學的基本概念，再介紹不同類型資料所應採用的各種計量模型。
本課程特別開設在上學期，主要的原因如下：
對於碩一的新生而言，修習這一門課可以儘早學習未來碩士論文所要進行模型估計的技巧，並儘早確認碩士論文的研究方向。
對於碩二的同學而言，可以在修習這一門課時，隨著上課的進度將碩士論文所要研究的資料，先將資料處理然後再進行估計，修完本課程也完成碩士論文實證資料的估計。
課程目標與學習成效:
有鑑於部分同學對計量分析的涉略不深，本課程的設計特點如下：
1.
由簡入深，降低進入門檻。本課程將先簡要複習統計學基本概念，而後說明計量經濟的研究方法，最後介紹近來發展的計量分析模型與運用。
2.
主要著重於觀念之解說與結果分析，減少數學方程式說明。
3.
配合導讀計量模型的相關文獻，說明各模型在經濟、政治、社會、國防與其他相關領域的應用，讓修課的同學瞭解量化分析研究的進行過程與撰寫方式。
4.
重視計量軟體之操作技巧與模型估計之分析，確保每位同學能實際操作電腦軟體。

課程簡介:
本課程為碩士班同學提供「議題導向」的學習：首先要學會提出有創意、有潛力的問題，然後學習用學術的方式解答。這學術的方式，是一種有系統思考的訓練，希望同學在任何場合，面對任何情境，都具備這樣的反思、透析真相、創意解決的能力。不要被閱讀書目嚇到。這些精彩的作品
不是
指定閱讀，而是日後寫論文時用得到的引用材料，透過課間概略介紹，可以先有一些概念。透過這個同學自己摸索的過程以及與老師一對一門診式的諮商對談，本課程將為同學即將來臨的學位論文寫作，找到具體方向，奠定良好的基礎。
課程目標與學習成效: 撰寫學位論文不只是完成個研究，而是學會掌握現象背後結構與運作邏輯的能力。以質性研究進行小範圍但深入探索的論文更是如此。在大數據分析日益盛行的當下，質性研究有何無可取代的價值？它看起來很容易入門，似乎人人都會，但不是「非計量」的研究就屬於「質性研究」。由於缺乏普遍認定的標準，質性作品普遍而言嚴謹度都不足，要能精彩，更屬吉光片羽。要操作已屬不易，要教會他人箇中難以言喻的技巧，更具挑戰。本課程即迎向此一挑戰，指導學員進行合於學術要求的質性研究。想像一個木雕師父，進行雕刻之前，第一步要認識材質。其次，當他拿到一塊木料，必須先知到是否是可造之材，價值為何（選題）；撫摸著木紋的，想像如何構圖，與成品的欣賞者對話；琢磨如何下刀（角度、力道），俾成就傳世的作品，把手中材料的價值極大化。此間，構思和雕刻技巧都是成就不朽作品的核心條件。要完成一個高明的質性研究與寫作也是如此，涉及許多難以言傳的默會知識，所有細節都要從操作中學習。然而，本課程希望能跨越這個障礙，有系統地瞭解研究設計背後的邏輯、各種研究工具的長處和限制、以及在田野中的人際互動等質性研究的重要元素，就能協助初學者迅速上手，減少犯錯的機會。本課程從比較哲學性的思考開始，檢視幾個主要的學派，掌握在理解人類社會現象時的關鍵議題，進而理解這些議題反應的研究方法上的基本主張。這些認識、構思與想像的訓練，能夠幫助初學者組合特定的調查方法進行研究設計，照顧好田野調查中的各項細節。本課程同時將教授論文撰寫與發表的技巧，順利把研究成果轉換成學術成就。

冷老師

李老師

本課程聚焦台灣的防衛戰略與AI時代下的整體防衛構想。課程首先討論台灣的防衛戰略，包括戰略一詞在軍事與政策脈絡下究竟該如何定義，台灣是否真正擁有一套整體戰略，還是僅止於分散的政策與武獲決策。課程會分析台灣所處的戰略環境，包括地緣位置、國際盟友關係，以及中國持續增加的軍事壓力，並比較國軍與共軍在戰略思維上的差異，說明雙方在資源配置、作戰概念與決策文化上的落差。
接著課程進入止戰的關鍵，討論如何在避免戰爭與嚇阻戰爭之間取得平衡。內容包括整體防衛構想（ODC）的核心邏輯、建軍優先順序與備戰整備現況，以及國防創新對提升嚇阻可信度的作用。課程也會引導學員思考台灣的防衛政策應該準備維持現狀到什麼時候，以及在兩岸關係與國際信任之間，台灣該如何建立堅韌的社會基礎，承受長期的灰色地帶壓力。
隨後課程進入AI時代的整體防衛構想，這是傳統防衛戰略課程比較少碰、但對未來十年很重要的主題。課程會說明軍事AI的能力光譜，涵蓋系統自動化、人類決策輔助、虛擬環境與實體世界的自主行動，並特別聚焦代理人式AI的興起。過去是人類提問、AI回答；現在則轉變為人類設定目標、AI自主規劃並執行，這個轉變重新定義了下一代戰力主導權的歸屬。課程也會討論當攻防雙方都掌握AI能力後，網路安全的競速邏輯會如何改變，零日漏洞的稀缺性正在下降，真正決定勝負的不再是誰先發現漏洞，而是誰能更快修補、隔離與復原。
最後課程回到具體的政策與實務層次，討論適合台灣的戰力整建與作戰構想，說明如何把前面談到的AI能力與防衛戰略思維，轉化為可執行的戰力優先順序。課程也會討論防衛韌性在社會、產業與國際能見度上的具體展現方式，並以台灣未來五年應該把握的關鍵決策路徑作為總結。

課程簡介: The Economics of Human Capital is a one-semester course at the senior-undergraduate or graduate level that offers a comprehensive examination of human capital accumulation. Topics include population dynamics, education and training, labor migration, entrepreneurship, nutrition and health, and gender. The course investigates the role of human capital in economic development by analyzing its properties and channels of accumulation through both theoretical frameworks and empirical evidence, with particular emphasis on economic reasoning and interpretation. Upon completion, students will understand the essence of human capital, its distinction from traditional physical capital, and its influence on labor market performance—both in terms of efficiency and equity—as well as on macroeconomic growth. Finally, the course addresses the effects of globalization and digitalization on human capital accumulation and income inequality.

課程簡介:
正確認識社會經濟性質，是思索社會問題並進一步提出解方的必要功課。當今國際社會中絕大多數國家是奉行資本主義的這套價值體系，因而也衍生出資本主義社會中的諸多社會/經濟/政治/文化/心理等問題與挑戰，例如傳統農業社會少見的雇傭關係，卻是資本主義社會中佔主導地位的關係，甚至具有支配地位，這個改變直接衝擊並超越民法體系的規範範疇，因為僱傭關係中的兩造當事人顯非民法的假設前提，故而後續才會出現勞動法體系的發展，其中明令禁止就業歧視，訂定最低工資/基本工資的保護，實施勞工保險，甚至在制定個體勞動法制 (如勞動基準法)之外，還要再來訂定集體勞動法制(如工會法、團體協商法、勞資爭議處理法，俗稱的勞動三法)。其次，傳統典型的勞資雇用關係在退潮中，取而代之的是各種非典型雇用的盛行，再加上數位經濟或平台經濟的興起，這對傳統以典型雇傭關係為藍本所建立起來的勞動法體系也構成極大的衝擊，各國仍在摸索因應解方。
這門課提供大家一個往根源處理解社會現象與問題的機會之外，將聚焦於介紹我國勞動關係與政策，同時比較國內外相關政策之內容與特色，例如比較德國、歐盟、國勞組織(ILO)或其他國家之發展策略，以助思考我國尚待改善與規畫之方針。課堂報告形式不拘，可自法律學、社會學、經濟學或政策層面提出討論。
課程目標與學習成效:

透過本課程，對於我國與各國因應當代勞動關係之問題與挑戰之處理方式與相關規範有基本認識。
經由本課程訓練研究能力培養撰寫報告能力，以及未來論文協作、閱讀外文之能力。

因應政經、社會及環境問題的快速變遷及複雜化之挑戰，有賴政府、企業及民間等公私協力的夥伴關係
(public-private partnership)
共同解決。為協助政府部門提供公共服務，並為維持作為社會價值缺口的支持性部門，及自主性運作，社會企業
(social enterprise)
因應而生，近年來更在全球各地欣起熱潮。疫情下，社會企業也發揮社會支持的功能，後疫情時代其發展更是可期。
在台灣社會企業的發展，政府已宣示
2014
年為「社企元年」，並整合相關部會部會現有政策，公佈了「社會企業行動方案
(103-105
年
)
」。以營造有利於社會企業創新、創業、成長與發展的生態環境；並於
2018
年核定「社會創新行動方案
(107-111
年
)
」，建立社會創新友善發展環境，發掘臺灣創新多元發展模式，並扣合聯合國永續發展目標
(SDGs)
之推動方向。
另針對國內區域及城鄉發展差距日益擴大，引發社會、就業、及環境的議題，政府大力推動地方創生，在地方創生國家戰略計畫中，社會參與創生是其中重要的推動策略之一，鼓勵及扶持地方社會企業創業，基於地方共好的目標，創造就業機會及促進地方經濟社會發展，達成均衡台灣的目標。
爰本課程將以環境永續及地方創生地等當前正要之社會發展議題為主軸，探討在後疫情時代，社會企業如何貢獻協助解決社會問題。
課程目標與學習成效:
社會企業專題的課程從宏觀與微觀的角度來探討社會企業的價值、趨勢、方法與實務。希望藉由觀念理論及方法的學習，案例的探討，以及創業計畫的演練，
培養學生對社會企業與趨勢及其應用的深度認知、養成專業能力及觀察技巧、掌握時下脈絡趨勢，以培育社會企業經營管理人才，及增進行政部門人才之社會企業專業知能。

課程簡介:
從
1980
年代開始，全球化成為最受到注目的發展趨勢，也是一個時代的潮流。在全球化的大屋頂之下，全球主要的經濟部門快速的融合，連帶的經濟整合的進程也為之挺進，歐洲聯盟快速的擴張，拉美國家持續推動（例如，南方共同市場、太平洋聯盟），而東亞國家在建立經濟共同體上也大步向前邁進（例如，
RCEP
）。
由於川普執意退出，使得
TPP
面臨到發展的困境，在日本領導下將之改造為
CPTPP
，
這展現出亞太國家仍努力於進行經濟整合。儘管如此，川普的路線和拜登政府無積極作為都使得國際社會懷疑美國對經濟整合的真正意圖。換言之，全球化逐漸的出現裂解。
值得注意的是中國大陸所扮演的角色。相對於美國川普總統追求重商主義的策略，重回到孤立主義路線，中國大陸卻是展現出擁抱自由主義市場經機，其主導的
RCEP
已經全面生效，且正式提出申請加入
CPTPP
，這使得東亞經濟整合未來的發展更具動態性，有許多可能的變化。尤有甚者，中國大陸在與其他國家簽署自由貿易協定已經開始逐漸升級，例如與秘魯、東南亞國協的自由貿易協定已進展到
3.0
，這更強化了其對整合的支持。而歐洲聯盟也在推動與其他國家或國家集團簽署自由貿易協定，例如，歐盟完成了與南方共同市場、日本的自由貿易協定，這都對經濟整合產生正面影響。這個發展趨勢不但影響到國家本身的發展，更在全球層次上衝擊到國際秩序的權力分配。
因之，本課程的設計一方面瞭解全球主義和全球化的意義、經濟整合的相關理論，另外一方面探討各區域整合進行的狀況，特別是比較西半球拉丁美洲國家及東亞國家在理論和實踐上的異同。值得注意的是影響全球化的兩大因素：其一是川普總統執意要重新建立以「美國再度偉大」（
MAGA
）為中心的國際貿易體系；其二是新冠狀病毒肆虐及俄烏戰爭導致國際供應鏈走向區域化的現象。我們也要探究這一現象，以及可能對經濟整合產生的影響。
課程目標與學習成效:
基於從
1980
年代到目前國際政治經濟情勢的快速變遷，本課程的目標使同學從理論上和實務上充分掌握此一轉換的流程趨勢及其內涵。透過自我學習、同儕思辮、以及老師的點評，期望同學能夠充分理解，並從政治經濟學的角度來分析並理解當前國際社會的頻繁互動、激烈競爭和無休止的爭霸。

本課程旨在介紹發展中國家國際關係研究，重大國際事件之發生經過和影響，課程並主要以大師級相關中文譯作作為課堂討論內容，以期培養同學對國際安全與國際政治經濟問題之獨立思考、分析能力。
同學修習本課程之預期收穫為：國際關係如何運作、政治與經濟如何交互作用、國際關係各種成員之間又如何互動及影響、以及我們應如何養成正確的國際觀，進而思考如何維護我國的外交與戰略利益，都是本課程所要探討的主題。
以課程講授為主，並隨堂抽問同學指定網站中外文資料及個人意見，此外亦要求同學在期中考週交付學期報告綱要，期末報告請於期末考週交付。
課程目標與學習成效: 發展中國家或譯為開發中國家，泛指南方國家和第三世界國家。就地理範圍而言，開發中國家一般包括亞洲、非洲和拉丁美洲的大部份國家。本課程亦以此項分類方式為準，分別說明相關區域的重大議題。不過發展中國家成員眾多，而且個別國家差異性極大，大國如巴西者，國土面積比美國本土(不包括阿拉斯加)還大，小國如亞太地區的海島國家，即使在地圖上也不容易尋找。有鑑於此，本課程將先從拉丁美洲國家和亞太國家切入，並對與我有邦交國家，作進一步的說明，俾使同學對相關發展中友邦有進一步的認識。此外本課程亦以美國著名政治學者杭廷頓(Samuel P. Hungtington)第三波民主化、文明衝突、誰是美國人，以及弗里曼(Thomas L. Friedman)世界是平的、世界又平又熱又擠、我們曾經輝煌等中譯出版品作為主要參考教材，以期同學從大師級著作中，擷取智慧的精華，從而形塑自己的世界觀。

課程簡介:
「不動產交易管理與法律專題研究」之課程，係以不動產交易過程中所涉及之主要法規作為研究對象，探討其理論與實務上有關之法律問題。由於我國並無一部稱之為「不動產交易法」之法律，故所謂不動產交易法係指「法律領域」而言。舉凡與不動產交易有關之法律，皆可納入此一法律領域，而本課程將篩選與不動產交易有關主要法規以為研析及討論。由於可能涉之法規甚多，本課程將以一學期探討一項法規之相關問題為原則。
本學期之研討主題為「不動產交易與公平交易法」。公平交易法是各產業市場競爭之遊戲規則，不動產交易相關產業之從業人員，對於此一經濟基本法亦應有基礎之認識。此外不動產交易案件中涉及諸多公平交易法上之問題，諸如不動產交易之不實廣告、不實促銷、資訊揭露以及對仲介業者之規範等，不僅對於事業之營業競爭行為甚為重要，對於購屋消費者之保護亦關係密切。熟悉公平交易法對於不動產交易之規範內容與理論實務，對於從事不動產交易之當事人可謂十分重要。本學期之課程內容，即在深入探討上述相關議題。
課程目標與學習成效: 本課程之目標在於使修習課程之同學瞭解公平交易法之基本架構、內容，以及公平法對於不動產交易之規範及理論實務。透過報告、討論及老師之說明講解，期盼在修完此一課程後，同學們能夠清楚掌握不動產交易與公平交易法之密切關連性，並具有處理相關問題之基礎法律知識。

課程簡介:
近年全球氣候變遷加劇，加以
COVID-19
疫情、俄烏戰爭及中東地區衝突等國際事件影響，導致全球糧食供應鏈受到衝擊，農業生產環境面臨嚴峻挑戰，糧食安全議題遂成為各國政府高度關注的重要課題。歐美國家逐漸體認農業除具有糧食生產功能外，亦兼具生態保育、環境維護、景觀塑造及社會文化等多元價值，因此透過農地利用規劃與農村發展政策，推動農業與農村地區之永續發展。

2016
年公布《國土計畫法》，將農業發展地區列為重要國土功能分區之一，以確保糧食安全、維護優良農地資源及農業生產環境為核心目標，並透過國土功能分區劃設、鄉村地區整體規劃及鄉村計畫等制度，強化農地利用管理與農村空間治理，避免土地零星開發及資源錯置利用。

課程簡介:
I. Course Objectives
This course is designed to help students understand the legal and governance issues arising from the development of digital technologies, with data governance as its central focus. It addresses major emerging topics, including personal data protection, artificial intelligence governance, digital platform accountability, open government data, data sharing, cybersecurity, cross-border data flows, and the European Union(EU)’s data governance framework.
Taught entirely in English, the course introduces students to core concepts in contemporary international technology law. It examines legal issues that arise throughout the data life cycle, from collection, processing, use, retention, and sharing to deletion. The course also considers the legality of artificial intelligence systems in model training and content generation, and analyzes the respective responsibilities and obligations of governments, businesses, digital platforms, and data intermediaries in data governance.
The course further incorporates Taiwan’s legal framework, the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Data Governance Act, Data Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, and other significant legislative developments and international trends. Through this comparative approach, students will develop a stronger interest in technology law and acquire the analytical skills needed to address practical legal issues.
II. Course Description
This course begins with legal issues related to data use as an entry point into technology law. It introduces key legal concepts, including personal data protection, informational self-determination, privacy, and data governance, before moving to issues such as open government data, data sharing, data intermediary services, data altruism, data access for Internet of Things devices and connected products, cloud switching, regulation of artificial intelligence technologies, algorithmic transparency, disclosure obligations, and legal requirements for cross-border data transfers.
The course focuses on recent developments in the EU’s data governance regime and explains how the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and Artificial Intelligence Act together shape a technology law framework grounded in trustworthiness, data access, and risk management. In addition to introducing major international technology laws, the course includes weekly case discussions to help students examine the relationship between data governance, personal data protection, public interest, industrial innovation, digital market competition, national data sovereignty, and the protection of fundamental rights.
課程目標與學習成效:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Understand the foundational theories and regulatory structure of technology law and data governance.
Examine legal issues concerning personal data protection, data sharing, digital platform regulation, risk-based regulation of artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity safeguards.
Compare Taiwan’s digital legal framework with the GDPR, Data Governance Act, Data Act, and other major technology laws of the EU.
Assess, from legal and governance perspectives, personal data protection risks and appropriate levels of regulatory oversight arising from artificial intelligence and other technological applications.
Analyze current disputes and cases involving the application of technology law from an independent perspective and propose appropriate legal or policy reforms.

課程簡介: This course examines the political economy of the global semiconductor industry through the analytical framework of geo-technology. Rather than focusing on technological or commercial aspects alone, it explores how semiconductors have become central to national security, industrial policy, global governance, and geopolitical competition in the post-globalization era. The first half of the course introduces major theories of international political economy, including neorealism, liberalism and developmental state theory, providing students with a strong analytical foundation. The second half compares the semiconductor development trajectories of the United States, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, and China, emphasizing the interaction between state capacity, industrial policy, and geopolitical change. Through comparative analysis and debates on issues such as the return of industrial policy and technological decoupling, students will develop critical analytical skills and a deeper understanding of the global political economy of semiconductors.

課程簡介:
This is a theoretically oriented seminar course focusing on the historiography, theories, and contemporary developments of linguistic anthropology, including the emerging linguistic anthropology of AI. The purpose of this course is to explore how linguistic anthropologists conduct research to foreground language practices within a matrix of cultural dynamics, power relations, social inequality, and identity construction. Different from formal analyses of language, linguistic anthropologists view language as social action through which meaning, language ideology, subjectivity, identity, voice, and power are constituted, contested, and transformed across time and space.
The course also examines how artificial intelligence, especially large language models and other AI-based language technologies, challenges and extends core questions in linguistic anthropology. AI-generated language raises important issues about interaction, communicative competence, authorship, voice, authority, knowledge production, and human–machine communication. By bringing classical theories of linguistic anthropology into dialogue with contemporary debates on AI, this course asks how language continues to mediate social life in an increasingly machine-mediated communicative world.

B. To train students to use core concepts in linguistic anthropology to analyze language as social action, through which meaning, language ideology, subjectivity, identity, voice, and authority are constituted, negotiated, contested, and transformed across time and space.

科目名稱: 治理中國：政治變遷、社會轉型與台港澳關係
英文科目名稱: Governing China: Political Change, Social Transformation, and Relation s with Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau

課程簡介:
This course examines the rise of China as the defining force shaping politics and society across the Greater China region. Over the past four decades, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has transformed from a poor, isolated polity into the world’s second-largest economy and a leading geopolitical power — with profound consequences not only for its own governance but for its relationship with Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, three societies bound to the mainland by deep cultural and historical ties yet possessing distinct institutional inheritances. The course asks: how has China’s rise reshaped the political institutions, social fabric, and external relationships of each of these polities, and what does the resulting variation tell us about the reach and the limits of Chinese-style governance?
The first half of the course maps the mainland system that drives these dynamics: major theoretical traditions for understanding Chinese politics (authoritarian resilience, fragmented and consultative authoritarianism, adaptive governance, party-state institutionalism); the organisation, ideology, and cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) under Xi Jinping; political change and policy implementation under the post-2012 leadership; the social transformation generated by urbanisation, hukou reform, demographic change, and growing inequality; and state–society relations including civil society, religion, ethnic politics, surveillance, and platform politics.
The second half traces how the rise of China has reshaped — and is being reshaped by — its peripheries. In Hong Kong, the asymmetric integration of the Special Administrative Region into the mainland’s political and economic order has accelerated since 2014, culminating in the 2020 National Security Law, the 2021 “patriots-only” electoral overhaul, and the 2024 Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (Article 23). In Macau, the rise of China has been managed through a quieter politics of accommodation, with deepening integration into the Greater Bay Area and continued reliance on a gaming economy increasingly aligned with Beijing’s strategic priorities. In Taiwan, China’s rise has driven both deepening economic interdependence (trade, investment, ECFA, semiconductors) and an intensifying security competition, with democratisation, identity politics, the 2024 presidential election, and the role of the United States all shaping the cross-Strait equation. The final two weeks are reserved for student case presentations.
課程目標與學習成效: By the end of the course, students should be able to: (1) compare leading theoretical models of Chinese governance and assess their analytical reach; (2) explain how the CCP organises power and recruits, monitors, and disciplines cadres; (3) trace the principal directions of political change under Xi Jinping; (4) analyse social transformation and state–society contention in mainland China; (5) compare the post-handover political trajectories of Hong Kong and Macau; (6) account for the trajectory of Taiwan’s democratisation and cross-Strait relations; and (7) deliver a research-grade case study and reflection note that engage critically with primary scholarship.

課程簡介: This interdisciplinary course explores Taiwan’s transformation from a marginal entrepôt trading deer hides to a key player in the global semiconductor industry. Through historical, economic, and technological lenses, it examines how foreign trade, colonial legacies, and global networks shaped Taiwan’s social and economic development. Topics include early maritime trade, Japanese colonial infrastructure, the rise of small and medium-sized enterprises, and Taiwan’s pivotal role in the global tech economy. The course also introduces foundational concepts in the history of science and traces the evolution of modern physics leading to the semiconductor revolution. Field trips and guest lectures enrich the understanding of Taiwan’s dynamic trajectory.
課程目標與學習成效:
To provide students with a historically grounded understanding of Taiwan’s role in global trade networks from the 17th century to the present.
To critically examine how colonialism, war, and industrial policy shaped Taiwan’s economic and infrastructural development.
To introduce key economic sectors—such as agriculture, transport, and manufacturing—and analyze their transformation over time.
To investigate Taiwan’s transition into a technological hub through the lens of science, education, and innovation.
To foster interdisciplinary thinking by connecting historical events with scientific advancements, particularly the rise of the semiconductor industry.
By the end of the course, students will be equipped to understand the broader socio-economic forces behind Taiwan’s development and its position within global capitalism and technological innovation.

課程簡介: This course surveys the discourses on hot wars, culture, gender, and sexuality in Cold War East Asia, and speaks to recent work in global “New Cold War” and historiography on the potential for rethinking the legacies of Cold War. The course strives to provide students with a strong understanding of some of the major actors shaping the development of states and the everyday experiences of people who lived in Asia during the period known as the Cold War. To this end, we will read scholarship on the legacies of imperialism and colonialism, Anti-Communism, Korean War, cultural and literary production on promoting Cold War ideology, and the gender/sexual politics in the artifacts or policies. Through the readings and discussions, we will challenge the existing world view of binarism, which is constructed by the ideology of Cold War Division (capitalism / communism, modern / tradition, gender dichotomy, progressive / backward…), and to approach a better understanding of the current geopolitical situation.
課程目標與學習成效:
Review important and classic works in the field of East Asian Cold War studies.
Investigating the histories of WWII, Korean War, and Vietnam War.
Understanding how the Cold War system operates, and is maintained through the norms of "sexuality/gender," and vice versa.
Understanding the issues and knowledge production of "Cultural Cold War" and "Cultural Imperialism".
Establishing preliminarily knowledge on "Cold War" and "sexual politics" in literary representations across East Asia.

In light of the prolonged Israeli-Hamas war and the ongoing tensions between the United States  and Iran, observers have warned of the possibility of a serious regional escalation and renewed global instability in the near future. The course “Ethnicity, Religion, Nationalism: Violence and the Politics of Belonging in the Global World” provides a structured space for students to critically examine how ethnic and religious identities shape nationalism and contribute to political conflict and violence in different regional and international contexts.
The course explores the interaction between religion and ethnic identities in Asia (East Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia), the Middle East, and the United States, and their impact on the construction of nationalism. It addresses critical questions of identity and citizenship, inclusion and exclusion, emotional and symbolic attachments, and the linkage between local and global political dynamics. The course asks how ethnicity and religion shape political interaction, how ethnic and religious identities may aggravate conflict or strengthen cooperation, and how they are mobilized in processes of nation-building and political legitimation. It further examines how relevant dimensions such as sacralization and symbolic forms of legitimation may lead to conflict and violence.
The course is divided into two parts. The first part introduces key concepts of ethnicity, religion, identity, nation, and nationalism, and examines major theoretical explanations for the emergence and persistence of nationalism. The second part focuses on the political consequences of nationalism for belonging and identity, including religious nationalism, fundamentalism, and identity-based conflict, through case studies from China, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, India, Turkey, Israel, and the United States.
The course also considers the role of digital technologies and artificial intelligence in shaping contemporary identity politics and nationalist mobilisation. Social media platforms, algorithmic systems, and AI-generated content increasingly mediate the circulation of ethnic and religious narratives, often amplifying polarization and reshaping boundaries of inclusion and exclusion in the process.
On Week 12 students will watch the film “Argo” (2012, Director: Ben Affleck)
,

religious leaders and practitioners to discuss the interplay between “religion” and “nationalism”, and conflict.

Understand the meaning of key concepts, such as ethnicity, religion, identity, nation, nationalism, religious nationalism and fundamentalism.
Understand the interaction and complex relations between these key concepts and their role in the politics of belonging and citizenship in various countries.
Understand the interaction and complex relations between these key concepts and their role in fundamentalism and/or political violence in various countries.
Be able to analyze current and/or past conflicts by examining how ethnicity and religion generate nationalism, which in turn may produce violence and political conflict in the global world.
Be able to critically assess how digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) shape the circulation, amplification, and contestation of ethnic, religious, and nationalist narratives, and how these processes influence contemporary forms of identity politics and conflict.

科目名稱: 人性與存有：民族誌與人類學觀點
英文科目名稱: Being Human: Ethnography and Anthropological Perspective
選課設定_限制與加簽: 開放低年級: 是 Yes｜非本院名額: 0｜總名額: 2｜開放加簽: 是 Yes
課程簡介:
The rapid development of artificial intelligence has created ethical debates about whether a robot, if one day it has self-consciousness, should be treated like a human being. Likewise, a growing demand for psychological therapies has resulted in/from the quest for meanings and purposes of being alive. Underlying these contemplations is a fundamental question: What makes a human a human? This course aims to facilitate discussions and provide potential answers from academic literature.
Based on anthropological theory, ethnography, and cross-cultural comparison, this course introduces the formation of human society, life stages, and the phenomenology of ‘being human’. In the past ten years, there has been a trend of thought in the humanities and social sciences, debating the social and personal aspects of the positive sides of social life, such as expectations, dignity, values, ethics, empathy, care, freedom, and hope. This course will examine the subjective and objective conditions of well-being, reflecting on how well-being is perceived, defined, and created. Through lectures, class discussions, student presentations on the required readings, and field trips/documentaries/guest speeches, this course attempts to cultivate students’ ability to care for society and themselves.
This course begins with introducing basic concepts and epistemology of anthropological theory and ethnography. We will unpack what anthropologists have called ‘culture’ and ‘society’ and consider how themes of this kind lead to a reconsideration of how anthropological theory and ethnographies might be useful for comprehending the development of humanity. After providing an overview, each week’s topic will focus on key issues discussed in the sub-fields of Cognitive and Psychological Anthropology, Medical Anthropology, Religious Anthropology, Environmental Anthropology, and Positive Anthropology. Throughout, this course will focus on the relationship between self and society and that between mind, body, and the more intangible aspects such as emotion and spirit. We will look at how universal human capabilities develop and are used during different stages of life to create unique cultural understandings and practices.
課程目標與學習成效: This course contains lectures, student presentations and in-class discussions. These activities are based on reading materials and the instructor's lecture slides. Apart from lectures, students are expected to summarise reading materials on the topic(s) they sign-up for at the beginning of the term and present their thoughts in the class (at least 1 presentation, depending on the class size). This course will emphasise analytical perspectives and critical thinking. Students are required to read before classes and bring their reflections and questions to in-class discussions. In addition to presentations, students are expected to write reading notes. Finally, this course encourages students to apply their knowledge to the real world by analysing a case related to the topics mentioned in this course. Students are expected to demonstrate their findings both in presentations and written works.

課程簡介: This course aims to provide students with a fundamental understanding of China's economic, social, and political development since 1978. Four main themes are involved. The first is the introduction. We will introduce this course with a discussion on the universality and particularity of the "China Model" from a comparative perspective. The second theme is economic transformation. We will explore China's industrialization and engagement with the world economy after the 1978 reform and opening up by examining the roles of the central government, local governments, the financial system, the fiscal system, state-owned enterprises, private enterprises, and foreign enterprises. The third theme is social changes. We will investigate the impacts that economic transformation brought to society in many aspects, including the urban-rural divide, social stratification, the one-child policy and its impact on demographics, as well as environmental issues. The fourth theme is political development. We will explore the implications of economic development for the prospect of democracy in China, as well as the impact that China's rise might bring to international political development. Moreover, we will show to and discuss with students selected movies related to the topics in the course, with an aim to improve students' understanding of some critical scenarios in the processes of China's political and economic development.
